💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Christmas market in England has been blasted by visitors after they discovered its AI-generated winter wonderland looked nothing like the real attraction.
  • In a recent development, kernow Christmas Market in Cornwall, England, promoted itself with AI images of bustling stalls surrounded by Christmas trees, garlands, and glowing lights.
  • Photos from the venue have also quickly spread across social media, showing vendors spread across a bare concrete floor beneath industrial lighting.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Christmas market in England has been blasted by visitors after they discovered its AI-generated winter wonderland looked nothing like the real attraction.

In a recent development, kernow Christmas Market in Cornwall, England, promoted itself with AI images of bustling stalls surrounded by Christmas trees, garlands, and glowing lights. However, instead of being met with bright lights and rows of Christmas trees, shoppers found themselves walking around a largely undecorated warehouse with a leaking roof.

Photos from the venue have also quickly spread across social media, showing vendors spread across a bare concrete floor beneath industrial lighting. It’s a far cry from the cheerful holiday imagery that the AI pictures depicted, and the organizers have now responded to the complaints and issued refunds to unhappy shoppers.

Recent findings suggest that kernow Christmas Market was being held at Pool Market as part of a wider Winter Wonderland attraction featuring an ice rink, Santa’s grotto and a funfair. However, one shopper told the BBC that the indoor market had “only about five stalls,” with no festive lights, decorations or Christmas music.

According to recent reports, the situation was particularly frustrating for vendors who had paid to sell their wares at the venue throughout the festive season. One vendor who spent £180 (around $240) on a pitch mentioned she arrived to find the warehouse undecorated. “It was just an empty space. There was nothing to suggest that there’s a market going on,” she said.

local Christmas market got advertised with AI, and this is what it looks like pic.twitter.com/IIWrhIjLH5.

Sources indicate that another vendor claimed businesses had been told to expect more than 50 stalls and over 2,500 visitors each day. Instead, they said the market was placed in a poorly advertised section of the warehouse with no signs directing Winter Wonderland customers towards it.

“They’ve told us we’re going to be part of this massive Winter Wonderland, 50-plus stalls, visitors of 2,500 people plus a day, then we get shoved in a dark corner of a warehouse,” they said.

AI fire detection system sprays food booth’s fake flames in bizarre viral video.

AI-Generated Christmas art removed after looking like “slop horror” scene.

Police forced to debunk “Killer” Cat in the Hat AI hoax spreading across the UK and Ireland.

The scenes have rapidly drawn comparisons to Glasgow’s infamous Willy Wonka experience, which also used AI images to attract visitors only to leave them disappointed by its lack of decorations and activities.

Recent findings suggest that “Not the Willy Wonka Glasgow debacle all over again,” wrote one commenter on X. “We got the Wonka Experience Sequel before Half-Life 3” joked another.

David Rowland, who organized Winter Wonderland and created the promotional images, acknowledged that AI imagery had been used to promote the market.

He mentioned they were meant to offer a “rough idea” of the planned experience rather than an exact representation of the venue. “You are never going to make it look exactly like the picture. It’s a lesson learned,” he said.

Rowlands Attractions has since confirmed that Kernow Christmas Market will accept no further bookings during 2026, while current bookings will be cancelled and fully refunded.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A woman said her ex-boyfriend called the police on her after he bought Grand Theft Auto 6 and she removed his access to her Xbox account, all so she could play.

Grand Theft Auto 6 was finally released on November 19, with an estimated 1.5 million people taking the day off in the United States so that they could experience Jason and Lucia’s story, as well as the wider state of Leonida.

However, shortly after release, a woman in Washington State revealed that her ex had called the police on her because she took her Xbox account back. In her TikTok, Ciara Benson noted that her ex, John, had access to her account for six years before she decided to lock him out.

Industry observers note that “Went in my account, removed all devices, signed out of everywhere, changed my password, added a restriction, it’s mine,” she said. “You don’t want to pay for your son? That’s fine. I got a new game, bitch.”.

Benson’s original TikTok has racked up close to 1 million views, but she also provided a follow-up too, revealing her run-in with police over it.

The TikToker remarked that her ex reported her for “credit card fraud,” which prompted officers to give her a call about it. “They did let me know that they did see the video I posted, so they were privy to the things going on,” she added.

Ciara also noted that she had removed all payment options from the account, seeing as they were not linked to her.

“He let me know that there was no evidence of a crime being committed that he could see, so they just gave me the incident report in case I need it. That was nice of them, very cool. The officier asked me how GTA was and if my son had played it.”.

Plenty of viewers have seen the funny side of her story, and even shared similar situations of their own. “My ex-husband tried to add a World of Warcraft character in our divorce stipulations,” one noted.

“911 is wild,” another added. “You should find someone that’s good at it. Let them play and send him updated screenshots of the game,” another joked.

Ciara said she hasn’t gotten “very far” with the missions just yet, but there is plenty of help out there for anyone struggling with GTA 6. If you need a fast car, there is a list of those, as well as the best weapons to use when you’re busting up some banks and stores for quick cash.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • EA FC will be adding AI-generated commentary from iconic football commentator John Motson, after gaining permission from his family.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you’re an EA FC (FIFA) player of a certain generation, then you grew up with Martin Tyler and Andy Gray providing the soundtrack to your games.
  • In a recent development, however, before all that, the BBC’s John Motson actually commentated on games for players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA FC will be adding AI-generated commentary from iconic football commentator John Motson, after gaining permission from his family.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re an EA FC (FIFA) player of a certain generation, then you grew up with Martin Tyler and Andy Gray providing the soundtrack to your games. In more recent years, that has shifted with Derek Rae, Stewart Robson, Guy Mowbray, and Sue Smith commentating on games.

In a recent development, however, before all that, the BBC’s John Motson actually commentated on games for players. ‘Motty’, who is synonymous with Match of the Day, was the voice of FIFA games from 1996 to 2006, before being replaced by Clive Tyldesley.

Now, the late commentator is set to return in EA FC 26, with AI-generated commentary lines coming from tools that have been “trained” on some of his iconic lines.

“My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,” Fred Motson noted.

“His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole latest set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.”.

EA SPORTS called it a “digital tribute” to Motson, with the option to start hearing the fresh commentary lines coming in the November 26 update.

As per the BBC, it is the first time that EA’s iconic series has included commentary lines from a deceased commentator.

“It’s not there to replace commentators in any way shape or form… there’s certainly no future aims to replace anyone with AI,” EA SPORTS’ Mat Prior also told them.

Once the revision goes live, you will have to change your commentary settings to hear Motson, but that’s a pretty simple thing to do.

An Umamusume clone that uses artwork closely resembling the game’s popular horse girls and racing features has appeared on the Google Play Store, leaving the community wondering how it managed to slip through the net.

From free browser games that combine Pokemon with Umamusume-style races to mods that replace Need for Speed Underground 2’s cars with horse girls, Cygames’ popular mobile game is constantly galloping its way into fan games and community projects.

The anime girl racing game has even sparked an upcoming competitor where players will duke it out against anime girls themed after iconic racing cars.

However, a fresh game has appeared on the Google Play Store using artwork that closely resembles Umamusume, with players branding it a “shameless” knockoff riddled with ads.

The game in question is Anime Racing Academy, a new app that was released on November 16 and has over 100 downloads. While there’s no gameplay shown off, developer HIFI PUBLISHERS has uploaded several screenshots of Anime Racing Academy to help give players a feel for what they can expect.

“Get ready for an exciting anime racing adventure in Anime Racing Academy! Experience thrilling racing challenges, compete on exciting tracks, and master your driving skills in this action-packed anime racing game. Enjoy fast-paced gameplay, smooth controls, and exciting racing competition,” reads the game’s official description.

According to recent reports, as you can see from the images below, the game looks eerily similar to Umamusume. There are images of horse girls running full speed across race tracks, idol performances where the characters sing after their victory, and training segments with Uma-style stats shown off.

Some players also download the game to see exactly what the “bootleg” version entailed, only to be left shocked by the amount of ads.

“I had the guts to download and play it. Holy f**king sh*t, what a sh*tty game. There are so many f**king ads that it took five minutes of loading and ads just to get through one race. Brutal,” revealed one player.

Interestingly, the developers have also uploaded another game titled Silver: Open World Detective, which appears to use promotional artwork from the upcoming gacha game Silver Palace.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Steam players will be able to vote for the best game of the past decade as Valve pits previous Game of the Year winners against each other in a upcoming award category.
  • To celebrate the 10th anniversary of the Steam Awards, Valve has introduced a special Hall of Fame gong for 2026, with the likes of Elden Ring, Baldur’s Gate 3, and GTA 5 all competing against each other.
  • Valve describes the new category as “a collection of previous Game of the Year award winners now in competition against each other for the title of #1 game of the past 10 years.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steam players will be able to vote for the best game of the past decade as Valve pits previous Game of the Year winners against each other in a upcoming award category.

To celebrate the 10th anniversary of the Steam Awards, Valve has introduced a special Hall of Fame gong for 2026, with the likes of Elden Ring, Baldur’s Gate 3, and GTA 5 all competing against each other.

Valve describes the new category as “a collection of previous Game of the Year award winners now in competition against each other for the title of #1 game of the past 10 years.”.

As a dedicated Game of the Year category didn’t exist on the platform until 2018, Valve has confirmed in an FAQ that winners of two other awards will serve as proxies for 2016 and 2017, those being GTA 5 and The Witcher 3.

It’s worth noting that both GTA 5 and The Witcher 3 were originally released in 2013 and 2015, respectively, and these appear to be enhanced and/or remastered versions released later.

Joining them are PUBG (2018), Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice (2019), Red Dead Redemption 2 (2020), Resident Evil Village (2021), Elden Ring (2022), Baldur’s Gate 3 (2023), Black Myth: Wukong (2024), and Hollow Knight: Silksong (2025).

Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards close on November 30 at 10 AM PT, with voting for the Hall of Fame award set to begin on December 17 alongside Steam’s Winter Sale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scientists were left stunned after finding a “surreal” site of kitchen appliances at the bottom of the ocean, all while they thought it was part of a shipwreck.

Recent findings suggest that oceans are, notoriously, one of the last places on Earth that haven’t been fully explored. The depths of some make it impossible for researchers to actually get a clear picture of what is lurking down there, even with all the money in the world being thrown behind some explorations.

Back in 2017, a group of researchers from NOAA, the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, had been using a ROV (remotely operated vehicle) in the Gulf of Mexico while looking for a shipwreck.

However, instead of finding ancient treasure, they stumbled upon a field of kitchen appliances on the seafloor, and couldn’t quite believe it.

In footage only released this year, almost a decade on, scientists from NOAA talked through their findings, with one expert calling it a “bit surreal” to see.

“We are at 1.5km in the deep sea, and here we are moving through a field of chest freezers, fridges, and washing machines,” they added.

Another joked that they’d “return this to the manufacturer and ask about the warranty,” when looking at one of the submerged washing machines.

Industry observers note that the debris had been found as the researchers picked up a “sonar target,” which they suspected to be a shipwreck. Instead, they found a 40-foot-long shipping container with a hole on the outside of it. It is certainly a unique find.

While the fridges and washing machines wouldn’t work on land, they had been put to work under the water, with the scientists finding coral growing on some, and fish also living around them.

Elsewhere, in Italy, divers discovered a 3,300-year-old sword stuck under a lake, and it was in “excellent” condition with a sharp blade too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red indicates the jump from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 will be comparable to the one Rockstar made between GTA 5 and GTA 6, with improvements planned for nearly every part of the game.

GTA 6’s launch has already drawn a reaction from CD Projekt Red, with Cyberpunk 2’s creative director joking that his own game was “cancelled” after seeing what Rockstar had pulled off.

However, the comparison came up again during CD Projekt’s earnings call, when the manufacturer was asked whether players should expect a similar leap from its next Witcher game.

As first reported by Eurogamer, CD Projekt Red co-CEO Michal Nowakowski remarked the studio had looked at what changed between Rockstar’s two games and that he expected The Witcher 4 to make a comparable jump.

Recent findings suggest that “We believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4, I think so, yes. It’s been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4,” said Nowakowski.

Nowakowski was also asked whether GTA 6’s launch would push CD Projekt Red to spend more on its own games. After all, GTA 6 is expected to have exceeded $1 billion in total development costs.

However, the CD Projekt Red CEO said the studio’s ambitions for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 had stayed the same.

“We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it’s [that it’s] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that’s for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 players who used the Upcoming Zealand trick to play early on PS5 may have inadvertently purchased a censored version of the game that’s missing a useful stamina buff.

With GTA 6 launching at midnight local time on November 19, impatient fans around the world used the Fresh Zealand trick to get a head start on their adventures in Leonida.

While Xbox players could simply change their console’s location, PS5 owners had to create a Fresh Zealand PlayStation account and purchase GTA 6 through the country’s digital storefront.

Unfortunately, getting into Vice City a few hours early appears to have come with an unexpected drawback.

As reported by IGN, Rockstar left out the ability to consume cocaine from your inventory in the Australian version of GTA 6, with Newly introduced Zealand reportedly receiving the same version.

In the international release, players can collect baggies of cocaine or skim some off larger bricks. Consuming cocaine through the item wheel gives players a supercharged stamina bar for roughly 30 seconds.

Australia’s video game classification rules allow depictions of illicit drug use but prohibit players from receiving gameplay benefits for taking them, even in games rated R18+.

Interestingly, Newly introduced Zealand doesn’t have this same restriction, but testing by GTA BOOM found that the mechanic was also absent from its New Zealand playthroughs.

Players had already suspected GTA 6 was censored in certain regions before launch when dataminers discovered a roughly 700KB discrepancy in the Australian and Latest Zealand game files.

Unlike Xbox people who temporarily changed their console’s location, PS5 players who bought the Newly introduced Zealand edition still own that regional copy even when playing on their regular account.

Luckily, those affected aren’t missing out on too much. Adrenaline can still be used to boost stamina and other stats, while scripted sequences involving cocaine remain intact.

Still, it’s a rather amusing twist that some of GTA 6‘s most impatient fans ended up with less content than those who waited a few extra hours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon has responded after one of its delivery drones crashed into a Michigan homeowner’s garage, prompting an investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

The incident occurred on November 20 in Huntington Woods, Michigan, after a couple placed an order for shampoo and received a notification that their package would arrive by drone within seven minutes.

Amazon has been expanding its Prime Air delivery service across the US, aiming to reach nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026. However, several crashes involving its drones have attracted the attention of federal regulators.

Speaking to WXYZ 7 News Detroit, Jim Brennan explained that the drone successfully dropped the package into his backyard before striking a fiber-optic cable and losing one of its propellers.

The aircraft then veered sideways before becoming trapped between his neighbor’s garage roof and nearby power lines.

“Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan remarked.

Logan Coomes, whose garage was struck, remarked an Amazon Prime Air team arrived within 10 minutes of the crash and worked with local utility workers to remove the drone by early evening.

The company reportedly offered to help repair the damaged roof and gave Coomes a $100 Amazon gift card.

In a statement shared with CNN, an Amazon spokesperson remarked its Prime Air drones conduct nearly 6,000 flights per day and have delivered “hundreds of thousands of packages this year.”.

Amazon also said the incident marked the first crash of its kind involving its drone delivery operations near Detroit.

The FAA published a preliminary incident notification on November 23, confirming that it was investigating the crash.

“UAS struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff,” the agency mentioned.

The National Transportation Safety Board is also gathering information but has not yet decided whether to launch a separate investigation.

Amazon’s battery-powered MK30 delivery drones are equipped with technology designed to detect and avoid obstacles and can carry packages weighing up to five pounds.

Industry observers note that the Michigan crash follows several other incidents involving Prime Air. In October 2025, two Amazon delivery drones crashed into a construction crane in Arizona, while another struck an internet cable in Texas the following month.

The FAA has also been investigating a separate crash involving an apartment building in Richardson, Texas, in February 2026.

Show, Don't Certify: How to Prepare for Your First Data Analyst Job

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Getting shortlisted for a junior data analyst job depends less on how many courses you have finished and more on what you can show.
  • Industry observers note that many people preparing for their first analyst role study for months and still struggle to get interviews.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

In a recent development, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Getting shortlisted for a junior data analyst job depends less on how many courses you have finished and more on what you can show. This plan breaks preparation into eight skill areas, pairs each one with a learning option and a hands-on task, and gives you a simple test for knowing when to move on.

Industry observers note that many people preparing for their first analyst role study for months and still struggle to get interviews. Their CVs list SQL, Excel and Tableau, yet nothing on the page shows those tools being used to answer a real question. Recruiters reading dozens of similar applications need something more concrete.

Recent findings suggest that A course can give your learning a sensible order, but a completion badge indicates little about how you think. A small analysis that states its question, explains its method and admits its limits tells a hiring manager far more. This initiative aims to collect that kind of proof while you learn, not after.

In a recent development, start by collecting ten to twenty entry-level postings in the industry you want to join, and tally the tools and tasks they mention. You will quickly see a pattern. Some roles are built around Excel and routine reporting, while others want SQL, a BI platform and a bit of Python.

It has been revealed that the wider market follows a similar shape. Jobright’s 2026 analysis of data analyst hiring, which looked at 2025–2026 postings from LinkedIn, Indeed and Levels.fyi, found that more than 80% of data analyst jobs mention SQL, over 60% mention Excel or Google Sheets, and roughly half mention Python or R. Let your own tally decide the order you learn in, but expect SQL to sit near the top.

As you work through each area below, finish with something you can show someone: a query, a tidied dataset, a chart, a one-page report or a portfolio project. Free material is often enough if you can stay disciplined. Pay for teaching only when it gives you something you cannot get alone, such as feedback, accountability or a fixed timetable.

SQL is how analysts pull, join and summarise records from a database, and a tool like Tableau lets other people explore what you found. Treat them as one workflow rather than two subjects: frame a question, write the query, sanity-check the numbers and present the result so a non-technical reader can follow it.

SQLBolt offers free, bite-sized SQL lessons that run in the browser, and Tableau publishes free training videos on connecting to data and building dashboards. Used together, they are enough to produce a small end-to-end project.

If you learn better with a set schedule and an instructor checking your work, you could learn to analyse data with SQL and Tableau from scratch through a guided programme at Heicoders Academy in Singapore. Whichever route you take, compare what is covered, how feedback is given, when sessions run and the full cost against what free resources already offer.

Proof you can show: A working SQL query set and your first published dashboard.

Move on when: You can take a question from idea to dashboard on your own, without following a tutorial line by line.

According to recent reports, spreadsheets are still where much of a team’s day-to-day reporting lives, especially when colleagues don’t write SQL. Get comfortable with filtering, pivot tables, and lookup functions, and learn to spot quiet errors like dates saved as text or one category spelled three different ways.

The next step is automating the cleanup so it doesn’t have to be repeated by hand each month. Microsoft’s Power Query documentation highlights how to import and reshape data in recorded steps that refresh when newly introduced data arrives. The same ideas apply in other spreadsheet tools too.

Proof you can show: A messy export turned into a summary that refreshes itself.

Move on when: You can clean an untidy CSV and build a report that updates when the source file changes.

For most junior analyst roles, the technical interview is a SQL test. Basic SELECT statements won’t be enough; interviewers like to probe joins, subqueries, common table expressions and window functions, which answer everyday questions such as running totals or each customer’s first purchase.

Practise with timed problem sets and review your answers for correctness as well as speed.

Proof you can show: Confidence going into a live or take-home SQL test.

Move on when: You can solve intermediate problems in around 15 to 20 minutes each without looking up syntax.

Take-home assignments often come with data that has been made messy on purpose. Reviewers want to see how you deal with missing values, duplicates and inconsistent formats, and whether they can follow your reasoning afterwards.

Sources indicate that keep a short cleaning log as you work, noting each change and why you made it. A separate sheet tab or a list of comments in a notebook both work.

Proof you can show: A take-home submission a reviewer can audit step by step.

Move on when: Every change to your dataset is written down with a reason.

Case-study questions test whether you can read numbers sensibly, not just produce them. A working grasp of distributions, means and medians, spread, correlation and sampling will keep you away from the mistakes that undo otherwise good answers, such as quoting an average that a few extreme values have pulled out of shape.

Proof you can show: Clear, careful answers in case-study interviews.

Move on when: You can explain in everyday language why two things moving together doesn’t mean one causes the other.

Every chart should help someone answer a specific question. Learn where bars, lines, scatter plots and simple tables each work best, and how axis ranges, labels and colour can nudge a reader towards the wrong conclusion. On a dashboard, the most crucial finding should be the first thing people see.

It has been revealed that datawrapper’s guidance on picking chart types is a useful free reference. As practice, show the same result in two different chart types and decide which one represents the data more honestly.

Proof you can show: Portfolio charts that make a point, not just show off features.

Move on when: A person who has never seen your data can spot the main finding and its caveat at a glance.

What counts as a useful metric depends on the role. Marketing analysts focus on conversion and retention, operations analysts on delivery times and capacity, and finance analysts on margins and cash flow. Choose one sector and learn exactly how its key measures are defined.

Proof you can show: A project built around the questions your target industry actually asks.

Move on when: You can define several sector metrics and describe how a manager would use each one.

Your portfolio is where the other seven areas come together. Two or three deep, well-documented projects will say more about you than a long list of quick ones. Give each project a README that sets out the question, the data, your method, the findings and the limitations.

Proof you can show: A portfolio link and a write-up you can talk through in an interview.

Move on when: Every project clearly explains what it asked, how you answered it and what you found.

There is no need to finish all eight areas before you apply. Once you can use the tools your target roles mention, speak honestly about your work and point to two or three clearly explained projects, start sending applications and keep learning alongside them.

Industry observers note that adjust each application to the job. Lead with a reporting example for spreadsheet-heavy roles, a query that solved a real problem for SQL roles, and a chart that supported a decision for visualisation roles. Be upfront about which work you built independently and which came from guided exercises.

In a recent development, do I really need eight courses? No. These are skill areas, not eight required qualifications. A single resource can cover several of them, and practice you do on your own counts as much as classroom learning.

Industry observers note that is it possible to prepare using only free material? Yes. Free tutorials, open textbooks, official documentation and public datasets cover the fundamentals well. The harder parts are sticking to a routine and finding people who will give you honest feedback.

Which should come first, SQL or spreadsheets? It depends on the jobs you want. Spreadsheets are an easy starting point for reporting roles, while SQL is expected wherever databases are involved. You will want both eventually, so start with whichever your target postings stress most.

How many portfolio projects should I have? Two or three solid ones are a good start. Each should show a clear question, steps someone else could repeat and an honest reading of the results, rather than several near-identical dashboards.

Do I need a certificate before I apply? Not usually. Some employers ask for one, but many judge skills through interviews, take-home tasks and tests instead. Go by what each posting actually requires.

It has been revealed that arellano had been missing since May 2025, when she disappeared from her home in Utah at the age of 15. She was allegedly held against her will in the basement of a home in Huntington, Oregon.

For Colorado teenager Landon Tresp, what began as an ordinary gaming session on October 15 would end with him helping a girl hundreds of miles away escape her alleged captor.

After meeting in Among Us, Landon and Arellano struck up a friendship and began communicating through Discord.

“We just kind of clicked,” Landon noted.

Over the following two weeks, Arellano began opening up about her situation, eventually sending Landon news articles covering her disappearance.

It has been revealed that realizing something was seriously wrong, Landon turned to his mother, Khristina, for help on Halloween. Neither knew that within 24 hours, the girl would finally be free.

Khristina began speaking with Arellano through Discord, but locating the teenager proved challenging as she didn’t know the address where she was being held.

“I knew I had to do everything I could to make sure she was brought to safety and had a second chance,” Khristina recalled.

Recent findings suggest that determined to find her, Khristina searched online property records before turning to real estate website Zillow. After being sent photos of two potential houses, Arellano recognized the second property.

Khristina contacted the girl’s family and began working with the FBI to bring her home.

On November 1, authorities arrived at the Oregon residence. Khristina stayed on a video call with Arellano, encouraging her to make the final few steps toward freedom.

For Landon, seeing the friend he had met just weeks earlier finally reach safety was an overwhelming moment.

“Oh my God, just pure bliss. I was so happy she was safe in that car. I was so happy she was out of that horrible monster’s house,” he said.

Despite everything that happened, Landon and Arellano haven’t stopped playing video games together.

The pair remain friends, while Khristina continues to speak with Arellano every day. The family is also hoping to meet her in person.

Recent findings suggest that A self-hosted LLM gateway sits between your app and the model provider, so every call pays for one extra hop. We measured that cost for three open-source gateways: the Langfuse AI Gateway, the LiteLLM proxy and AcruxCore. Each one ran on the same machine, in front of the same OpenAI model. LiteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to every non-streaming call. AcruxCore added 15 to 24 ms. Langfuse's number could not be told apart from zero.

In a recent development, the bigger lesson was about the measurement itself. Before we controlled for it, one OpenAI network address moved our results by more than any gateway did.

Sources indicate that each number is the median time a gateway added to a direct OpenAI call, with its 95% interval in brackets. A gateway can log each call, and logging takes time, so we ran the test three times with three logging levels.

Sources indicate that the direct call took 781 to 831 ms at the median, so even LiteLLM's cost is under 9% of a short call. Read the tables this way:.

According to recent reports, the obvious test is to time 100 calls through the gateway, time 100 direct calls, and compare the two medians. That test gives the wrong answer, for two reasons.

According to recent reports, the first reason is noise. OpenAI's own response time moved by hundreds of milliseconds between calls in our runs. The direct call's p95 was 1,047 to 1,233 ms against a median near 800 ms. A gateway that adds 20 ms is hidden inside that spread unless the test removes it.

The second reason is the network path to OpenAI. It does not stay the same between a direct client and a gateway, and that difference can be larger than the gateway itself.

Recent findings suggest that api.openai.com resolves to more than one address. From our network, DNS returned two Cloudflare addresses, and one was much farther away than the other. We measured both with a script that pins one address at a time:.

Recent findings suggest that on a connection that is already open, both addresses answer in the same time. On a newly introduced connection, the far address adds about 250 ms, because the TCP and TLS handshakes take that much longer.

A gateway keeps its connection to OpenAI open between calls. It pays the setup once and then stays on whichever address it reached first. A client that opens a new connection for each call pays the setup again on every call. How much it pays depends on which address DNS returns that time.

It has been revealed that node's built-in fetch closes an idle connection after about 4 seconds. So a test client that calls OpenAI every few seconds reconnects on almost every call. In our first, uncontrolled run, the Langfuse gateway came out 43 ms faster than calling OpenAI directly. A gateway cannot be faster than the call it forwards. The direct client paid for new connections, and the gateway did not.

The fix has two parts. First, pin api.openai.com to one address on every path. In Docker, that is an extra_hosts entry on each gateway container:.

It has been revealed that second, let the direct client keep its connection open, as a gateway does. With undici, the HTTP client behind Node's fetch, that is a custom Agent:.

We then listed each container's open connections to confirm that every path used the same address. The edge-check script is in the repository linked at the end, and it takes about a minute to run from your own network.

In a recent development, this advice also applies outside benchmarks. If your app calls OpenAI directly from Node, keep the connection open between calls. Otherwise some of your calls pay the handshake, and on a far address that costs about 250 ms.

Industry observers note that each test sent 150 rounds after 5 warm-up rounds. One round calls OpenAI directly and through each gateway, once without streaming and once with streaming. The order rotates every round, so no path always goes first or last.

In a recent development, for each round, the script takes the gateway's time minus the direct call's time in that same round. Calls in one round are made within a few seconds of each other, so a slow moment at OpenAI hits all four paths together and cancels out of the difference. The script then reports the median of the 150 differences.

The interval comes from a bootstrap. The script draws 150 differences at random, with replacement, and takes their median. It repeats that 2,000 times, and the middle 95% of those medians is the interval. This is a shortened version of the script's function:.

It has been revealed that an interval that includes zero means the test could not separate the gateway's cost from zero. That is what the Langfuse rows show. It does not prove that the cost is zero.

According to recent reports, every call used OpenAI gpt-6-luna with reasoning_effort: "none", the same short prompt and a cap of 5 output tokens. A short answer keeps the model's own time small, so more of the measured time belongs to the path. Each streamed call measured the time to its first token. Each non-streamed call measured the time to the full response.

All three gateways did real work on every call, which made the comparison fair:.

The three logging levels mapped to these settings:.

Industry observers note that the machine was an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X with 62 GB of RAM, running Fedora Linux and Docker 29.9. All three stacks ran on it at once, and the test was run on 10 November 2026.

Sources indicate that liteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to the full response, but only 9 to 43 ms to the first streamed token. The first token arrives as soon as the model starts to answer, so time spent before that point demonstrates up in both numbers. The larger cost without streaming suggests that most of LiteLLM's extra time is spent after the model has answered. We did not profile LiteLLM to confirm this.

In a recent development, logging level made no clear difference for any gateway. Adding LiteLLM's Langfuse callback did not raise its cost. AcruxCore's median rose from 15 ms with logging off to 24 ms with full logging, but its intervals overlap across all three runs. AcruxCore's median is 16 to 24 ms above Langfuse's, and those intervals overlap too, so this test does not rank the two of them.

According to recent reports, if 60 ms per call matters to you, as in a chat app that makes several model calls per user message, LiteLLM's cost is real and repeatable. Langfuse and AcruxCore stayed near or within the noise. If your calls take several seconds, any of the three costs less than OpenAI's own variation from one call to the next.

Recent findings suggest that before you trust a gateway number, your own or anyone else's, check two things. Was each gateway compared with a direct call in the same round? And did the direct client keep its connection open on the same OpenAI address as the gateway? Without both, the result measures the network path and not the gateway.

The scripts, Compose files and raw results are on GitHub: scripts/comparison/langfuse-gateway-vs-litellm-vs-acruxcore.

However, a website called PlayMyPS5 is giving players another way to experience Vice City without having to purchase the game or a console, while attempting to get the internet to complete its story together.

PlayMyPS5 broadcasts gameplay directly from a physical PS5, allowing visitors to join a public queue and remotely control the console through their web browser.

Each player is given five minutes to play before control is handed over to the next person in line. Players have 20 seconds to claim their turn, while remaining idle for 30 seconds will bring their session to an early end.

The website supports controllers, keyboard and mouse, and mobile touchscreen controls. Players can also watch others explore Vice City and communicate through a live chat while waiting for their turn.

There are no downloads, payments, or registration requirements to join the queue, and players can rejoin once their session ends.

Sources indicate that the project was created after its developers realized their PS5 spent much of its time sitting unused. Now, they’re encouraging visitors to work together to complete every GTA 6 story mission.

The creators are also attempting to raise $993 to purchase a second PS5, allowing more people to play simultaneously and reducing queue times. Other PS5 owners with a copy of GTA 6 can volunteer to share their consoles through the platform.

The pages of a site form a graph. Think of it as many nodes connected to each other via edges. Each of the edges are the links between the pages, and the nodes themselves are the pages. Now if you start to visualize this as a graph, you will promptly see that there are multiple ways to traverse this graph and reach a particular endpoint.

A search crawler usually uses one of these pages as a starting point and crawls through all of the pages (especially when pages are not fully covered in a sitemap).

Sources indicate that if a page lies very deep from the home page, it means that it's not an key page. It's an indication to the search engine that this is not something that you yourself consider important, and the search engine has a lesser incentive to rank this page over pages that are linked better within your site.

Sources indicate that the key metric here is link depth. That is the number of clicks it takes to reach a particular page from your home page.

Another key metric is broken links. If you have too many broken links, it indicates to the search engine that your site is outdated and not well maintained, and the search engine will then not want to rank your site.

The way to identify both these problems is the same: to actually walk through your site, do a crawl of your site outside in, and try to figure out what the link depth is and if there are broken links on your website.

Recent findings suggest that seed the crawl with the home page and all URLs mentioned in the sitemap. Technically, the sitemap is not required if you're doing a crawl, but going from the sitemap will allow us to detect orphaned pages as well.

Sources indicate that fetch the pages and follow redirects as required. Record when you're following a redirect: we do not let fetch follow it silently, we record each hop and add its target to the crawl. Record HTTP errors as they occur.

Drop URL fragments and tracking parameters. Keep trailing slashes because sometimes there can be mismatches around expectation of trailing slashes in different URLs of a site.

Sources indicate that in order to navigate from the home page, we can use BFS. So we know that the first time we reach a page, that is the page's shortest path.

We can cut off the depth over a certain threshold, say 5, to indicate that pages beyond that are too far or too deep to be reached.

Noindex pages will still be crawled. However, we need to make a record of them being not indexed, to reflect that they will not be present in the search engine.

The desired page depth is as close to the home page as possible. Key pages should be close to the home page. The deeper you go from the home page, it signals to the search engine that the page is less important.

A couple of examples of how a deep page is present:.

The suggested fix for this is that we link the pages from as close to the home page as possible:.

Wasted links are those internal links that do not do the job they're supposed to do. The different types of wasted links:.

We have seen here how to look at our own website through the lens of a search engine. You can use some of the code over here to create your own crawler and identify internal linking issues; the full script is in this gist. Alternatively, we can use a free internal link visualizer to identify these issues and focus only on the fixes to improve our site's internal linking.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 103-year-old gaming grandmother is taking part in a Tekken tournament, with one of her closest rivals also being 95 years old.

Sources indicate that even though gaming, and especially esports, are seen as a hobby for the younger generation, there are plenty of older folks who get involved as well. Those who grew up on the likes of the PlayStation One, Atari 2600, NES, and even the Sega Genesis still want to be involved.

Over in Japan, the Care Esports Association runs competitive gaming events aimed at senior citizens throughout the year, with an annual event taking place in December around Tekken 8.

Typically, competitors are aged between 70 and 90, but this year, they’ve cracked the 100-year-old mark, with a 103-year-old grandmother taking part.

As per Denfaminico, 103-year-old Toshiko Morishita will play in this year’s event, which is also looking to set a Guinness World Record for the “highest average age of esports tournament participants.”.

According to the outlet, the 103-year-old knows that her age might be a barrier to success, but said that even losing would still be “enjoyable” for her.

She “enjoys the game” without “being solely focused on winning or losing,” but has been putting in practice to prepare for the event.

As noted, competitors at the event typically range from 70 to 90 years old, with last year’s winner – Hisako Sakai – clocking in at 92 years old.

Sakai fought her way to first place using Claudio Serafino and defeated 95-year-old Sadayuki Kato in the semifinals.

The average age at last year’s event was just under 87, so having a 103-year-old competing will drag that up – hopefully, for them, into Guinness World Records territory.

On the other end of the scale, a five-year-old Tekken player drew attention for playing in a tournament, seeing as the game is rated for teenagers. Harada gave him a pass, though, saying he has a “bright future.”.

  • Japan is expanding its AI crackdown on manga and anime piracy overseas after testing a system that can find websites hosting unauthorized copies.
  • On November 24, The Yomiuri Shimbun reported that Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs found pirated manga on 94% of the 1,935 websites its AI flagged for suspected manga piracy.
  • For its overseas tests, the agency trained the AI to recognize domain names commonly associated with piracy sites and could compile the results as early as March 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan is expanding its AI crackdown on manga and anime piracy overseas after testing a system that can find websites hosting unauthorized copies.

On November 24, The Yomiuri Shimbun reported that Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs found pirated manga on 94% of the 1,935 websites its AI flagged for suspected manga piracy. Of the 1,564 sites flagged for suspected anime piracy, 89% hosted unauthorized copies.

For its overseas tests, the agency trained the AI to recognize domain names commonly associated with piracy sites and could compile the results as early as March 2027.

Japan’s latest anti-piracy push follows an April 3 discussion in the country’s House of Representatives, where executives from some of Japan’s biggest animation studios warned that piracy remains one of the biggest obstacles to anime’s growth overseas.

Among them was Toei Animation, the studio behind One Piece and Dragon Ball, which called for stronger government action on anime piracy.

According to data published by Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry, piracy losses from digital content rose from two trillion yen in 2022 to 5.7 trillion yen in 2025, increasing from roughly $13.3 billion to around $38 billion USD.

In a bid to curb those losses, Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs has also expanded its AI piracy tests to target overseas sites hosting unauthorized copies of manga and anime, with aims to compile its findings as early as March 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 caused a pretty major drop in real-life gym workouts, with new data revealing just how much people focused on working out in-game instead.

On November 19, Grand Theft Auto fans finally got to get their hands on GTA 6, quickly diving into Jason and Lucia’s story, as well as exploring the wider state of Leonida.

Even though the game has been out for a week, plenty of players have not progressed past Chapter 1. Many have lapped up the enjoyable vibes of Key Lento, playing pool at the Rusty Anchor, focusing on fishing off the coast, and working early missions for Brian Heder.

Recent findings suggest that one key part of the first chapter, and those there after, are workouts. Jason’s deck has a partial gym setup, and there are fully fledged gyms elsewhere in Vice City.

Well, as it turns out, plenty of people decided to focus on Jason’s workouts rather than their own following the game’s release.

Industry observers note that as per stats from Gymverse and Fitness22, workouts logged by Gymverse consumers dropped in substantial ways. The biggest drop came in Saudi Arabia, as numbers dropped by 17%. In the UK and United States, the drop in logged workouts came in at 12% in the first 24 hours of the GTA 6 launch.

Over the first three days of the launch week, though, worldwide workouts dropped by 10% compared to the weeks before.

“Our data suggests that for three days, many people chose to work out in Vice City rather than in the gym,” noted Yossi Tarablus, VP of Marketing, Fitness22.

It has been revealed that it wasn’t just workouts and gym numbers that were impacted by the launch. An estimated 1.5 million people in the United States took at least one day off to play GTA 6. That was said to cost the economy around $1 billion.

Unlike in GTA, there is no real cheat code to bulk up in real life other than putting in the hard work.

Industry observers note that running an AI agent on your own GPU sounds simple: point it at Ollama and stop paying per token. I set up OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, with a 9B model in Ollama on one RTX 3090 and connected it to Discord. Then I read the Ollama log for every request.

In a recent development, the agent worked. The numbers were not what I expected, though. A one-line question turned into a prompt of more than 18,000 tokens, the first reply took over a minute, and the small model sometimes guessed instead of using its tools.

This article covers what I measured and what each number means if you plan to run an agent on local hardware.

In a recent development, openClaw ran in Docker and reached Ollama on the host at http://host.docker.internal:11434. Discord was the chat interface, and OpenClaw's web panel revealed the sessions and context use.

This article is about the results, not the installation. The full step-by-step setup is in a separate guide to running OpenClaw in Docker with Ollama and Discord. That guide covers the Compose file, the Discord bot and how to keep the ports off your network.

All timings below come from the Ollama log on the test machine. Ollama loaded the model with a 32,768-token context.

My first message in Discord was short: "Which model are you running on, and what is 17 * 23?" The bot answered correctly: it ran on ollama/qwen3.5:9b, and 17 × 23 is 391.

In a recent development, the Ollama log demonstrated what that question cost. The model processed 18,415 prompt tokens and generated 33 tokens.

Industry observers note that the extra tokens come from the agent itself. With every request, OpenClaw sends:.

On the RTX 3090, reading that prompt took 10 seconds at 1,838 tokens per second. A slower GPU, or a CPU, needs much longer to read the same prompt.

According to recent reports, prompt tokens per model call, from the Ollama log. Only the first message had to process the whole prompt.

OpenClaw counts tokens with its own estimate, which was higher than the Ollama count. The gateway log estimated the prompt at 24,608 tokens, against a prompt budget of 24,576 tokens for this model. By OpenClaw's own count, the base prompt alone used up the budget before any conversation history.

The web panel showed a similar figure: 68 to 69 percent of the context window was in use for the Discord sessions after only a few messages.

Sources indicate that the first message arrived while the model was not loaded in GPU memory. That reply took 1 min 10 s:.

The next requests were much faster:.

Industry observers note that reply times on the test machine. Loading the model took most of the first reply.

According to recent reports, the speed-up comes from prompt caching. The system prompt, tool definitions and workspace files at the start of the prompt stay the same between requests. Ollama kept that part cached and processed only the latest tokens. The model wrote at 91 to 96 tokens per second in every test.

Ollama's documentation says models stay in memory for 5 minutes by default before they are unloaded. After that, the next message pays the load time again. You can change this with the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable on the Ollama server, or with the keep_alive parameter per request. A negative value, such as -1, keeps the model loaded. I did not change this setting in the test.

If you run Ollama in Docker, pass the variable with -e OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 or in the environment: section of your Compose file.

Two things used the GPU besides my chat messages.

According to recent reports, A heartbeat. OpenClaw's web panel listed one scheduled automation, heartbeat-main, which runs every 30 minutes. The agent wakes on that schedule, so the model gets called even when nobody chats. With Ollama's 5-minute default, the model is unloaded between heartbeats unless someone chatted recently, so a heartbeat most likely starts with a model load. I did not measure this.

Industry observers note that an embedding model. During the first message, OpenClaw also called Ollama's /api/embed endpoint twice to index its memory. It used qwen3-embedding:4b, which was already installed on the Ollama server. I did not set OpenClaw to use that model; it picked it on its own.

The two models took this much GPU memory:.

That is 11.4 GB for the models alone, almost half of the RTX 3090's 24 GB.

The rest of the stack was light:.

Recent findings suggest that what this means for you: blueprint GPU memory for the chat model, the embedding model and the context, not the chat model alone. If the GPU also runs other models, the heartbeat can compete with them.

The first two tests in Discord: a question, then a file written with a tool. The user name is blurred.

The mistakes demonstrated up when the model had to check something:.

According to recent reports, after the restart, the bot claimed it had lost the earlier session. When asked to use its read tool, it read the file correctly.

In a recent development, the fix for the first problem was simple. When I wrote "use your read tool to open homelab-test.md", the model opened the file and listed all three points correctly. Naming the tool made it check instead of guess.

The model listed four files and missed the test file and a folder, because it answered from its prompt.

Based on this test, a local 9B model on one consumer GPU works for:.

If you need better answers, OpenClaw also works with hosted models, but then your prompts leave your machine.

In this test, qwen3.5:9b used 6.3 GB and the qwen3-embedding:4b memory model used 5.1 GB. Together the two models needed 11.4 GB.

Sources indicate that the model had to load into GPU memory first, which took 59 seconds of the 70-second reply. Ollama keeps a model loaded for 5 minutes by default, and the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE setting changes that.

Every request includes OpenClaw's system prompt, its tool definitions and its workspace files. A one-line question became an 18,415-token prompt in this test.

Yes. A heartbeat automation runs every 30 minutes and calls the model even when nobody sends a message.

In a recent development, it handled questions, arithmetic and file creation correctly in this test. It sometimes answered from its prompt instead of using its tools. When it wrongly remarked its memory was lost, asking it to use its read tool made it check the file and answer correctly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A runaway horse in Virginia made an unexpected trip to McDonald’s before leading police on a chase through a residential neighborhood.

On November 17, police in Colonial Heights were called to a McDonald’s after a horse named Rolo was spotted wandering along a busy road.

The horse had escaped from Hickory Haven Equestrian in South Chesterfield after managing to roll underneath an electric fence.

Speaking to 12 On Your Side, owner Ashley Moyer explained that she believes the restaurant’s lights and the presence of people may have attracted Rolo.

“McDonald’s is a pretty straight shot,” she said.

Moyer also revealed that this wasn’t the first time the horse had escaped from the equestrian center, joking that “Rolo is a repeat offender.”.

Two Virginia State Police troopers who were heading home from work encountered the horse while local officers were already in pursuit, joining efforts to bring the animal to safety.

Dashcam footage released by Virginia State Police shows officers following Rolo as he makes his way through the area before eventually being cornered at Shepard Stadium.

Officers used lassos to secure the horse, with one officer helping to keep him calm until he could be reunited with his owner.

“Using a little teamwork, some lassos, and the power of friendship, everyone worked together to safely corner and wrangle our four-legged runaway away from traffic,” Colonial Heights Animal Control said in a Facebook post.

Rolo’s owner was alerted to his escape after receiving several phone calls in the middle of the night, followed by a police officer knocking on her door.

It has been revealed that “He just kind of hung out and walked behind. We had a police escort on the way back … and he seemed to enjoy his walk,” Moyer said, as reported by People.

In a Facebook post, the equestrian center thanked the officers involved in Rolo’s capture, joking that despite escaping his enclosure, the horse had been a law-abiding road user.

“The good news… Evidence indicates that Rolo obeyed all traffic laws on his road trip, even coming to a complete stop at the sign,” the center said.

A woman has gone viral after being forced to jump into a stranger’s car by a pack of wild turkeys, with the helpful driver calling them “bullies” as well.

Industry observers note that getting chased by animals when you’re going about your day can, at times, be a pretty traumatic and scary experience. This is especially the case when it’s a bigger animal or scarier breed.

However, on November 21, a woman went viral after she was caught being chased down a street by a pack of wild turkeys. Taryn Laprade told WHDH that she and her pastor had taken a wrong turn and spotted the woman being chased in Newton, Massachusetts.

Industry observers note that “Are they trying to get you?” the pastor shouted out. “They’re gobbling at her!” a surprised Laprade added. The woman begged for the pair’s help as more and more turkeys kept on following her as well.

Recent findings suggest that “Were you feeding them?” the man asked as the unnamed woman jumped in the car. Laprade and her pastor offered to give her a short ride away from the “aggressive” animals as well.

It has been revealed that “It was bizarre. I’ve never seen anything like it before. I see turkeys all the time, but I’ve never seen turkeys aggressive like that, I mean, they were right on her,” Laprade told WHDH.

“Afterwards she thanked us and kept telling us, ‘You saved my life.’ She was very, very grateful that we pulled up.”.

According to the report, the woman did not sustain any injuries during the ordeal, and neither did any of the turkeys. It was just a scary moment for her.

Elsewhere, a horse in Virginia stopped off at a McDonald’s after it managed to escape from an equestrian centre. Police were led on a wild chase by the horse, which was eventually stopped and led back to its stable.

Tech Report: Rockstar explains why GTA 6 added its Criminal Profile system

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (482 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games’ head of development has explained why GTA 6 tracks how players commit crimes, saying the idea grew out of lessons the studio learned while making Red Dead Redemption 2.
  • Unlike previous GTA games, GTA 6’s protagonists each have their own Criminal Profile that changes based on how they behave across Leonida.
  • Pulling off robberies without unnecessary violence can move a character toward Professional, while attacking civilians and going on prolonged rampages can push them toward Irredeemable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games’ head of development has explained why GTA 6 tracks how players commit crimes, saying the idea grew out of lessons the studio learned while making Red Dead Redemption 2.

Unlike previous GTA games, GTA 6’s protagonists each have their own Criminal Profile that changes based on how they behave across Leonida.

Pulling off robberies without unnecessary violence can move a character toward Professional, while attacking civilians and going on prolonged rampages can push them toward Irredeemable.

These ratings then impact how aggressively police respond and how each character replenishes their Focus meter, the latter being key for improving your aim in gunfights.

While the consensus on the latest system has been mixed amongst the community, Rockstar Games’ head of development Rob Nelson has now revealed the reasons behind its inclusion.

Speaking to Eurogamer, Nelson said Rockstar wanted to bring what players do in the open world closer to how Jason and Lucia are portrayed in the story.

Recent findings suggest that that meant giving players more choices in everyday encounters, right down to normal GTA actions like robbing an NPC. Nelson mentioned the team was aiming to “build up the sophistication of the NPC population, and also allow for more player choice” while also adding “more options in terms of the way you interact with the world beyond just violence.”.

Sources indicate that after all, the results of going on a rampage in GTA 6 can follow you long after you lose the cops. In fact, repeated acts of extreme violence can permanently lock your Criminal Profile at Irredeemable. However, Nelson mentions that it also allows for further freedom in your actions.

According to recent reports, “It’s still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don’t have to beat them to death to get their money,” Nelson explained.

Rockstar also wanted to create a more realistic approach to player actions, building upon Red Dead Redemption 2’s Honor system.

Sources indicate that “What if, instead of whipping an RPG out of nowhere, you have to call your car. You have to pop a car trunk and get it, and now I’m walking, and now people are noticing, but they’re sort of sidling away, and it’s more believable,” the developer continued.

“[Now] there’s people who also have guns, and they’re shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up, and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them.”.

It’s certainly a bold change for a series built around causing chaos, but it’s part of the reason why GTA 6 feels so much more alive than previous titles. So much so that Cyberpunk 2’s creative director even joked that the sequel is “cancelled” after seeing what Rockstar has achieved.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

In a recent development, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Picking an ecommerce platform is really a decision about which layers you want to own: the storefront, the catalog and order logic, the payment flow, and the hosting underneath. Every platform below draws that line in a different place. If you have already settled the front-end question with a comparison like SitePoint's Astro vs Next.js guide, the next question is what sits behind it. Prices are from each vendor's pricing page as of November 2026.

According to recent reports, shopify is the fully managed option. Basic costs $29 a month with card rates from 2.9% plus 30 cents, and a 2% fee applies to orders processed through a third-party gateway on that plan. Developers get two routes: Liquid themes, or Hydrogen, Shopify's headless toolkit, where your framework owns routing and rendering and Hydrogen supplies the Storefront API client and cart. Templates exist for React Router on Oxygen and for Next.js on Vercel. Plus starts at $2,300 a month.

Whop is a business platform for taking payments and sending payouts, and it sits under a storefront you have already built rather than replacing it. The Checkout element runs in the browser with no server code and no API key on the page. You pass your own order ID as metadata, Whop copies it onto the payment, and your server fulfills from a signed webhook that follows the Standard Webhooks spec. Domestic cards cost 2.7% plus 30 cents with no monthly fee, buyers see payment methods chosen by their location across 195 countries, and the same balance pays out in over 200 countries, including to affiliates or sellers you onboard. Whop's own guide shows how to integrate a checkout API into a Next.js storefront end to end. The trade-off is that there is no catalog or shipping engine; you collect address fields at checkout and trigger fulfillment from the webhook.

It has been revealed that wooCommerce is a free plugin on WordPress you host yourself, so you own updates, security, and performance. Its payment gateway, WooPayments, charges US merchants 2.9% plus 30 cents per card transaction, 1.5% more for international cards, 2% for currency conversion, and $25 per dispute. Everything is PHP hooks and filters, which makes it the natural pick for agencies already living in WordPress and the wrong pick for anyone who does not want to run a server.

In a recent development, bigCommerce hosts the back end and lets you bring any front end. Core is $29 a month billed annually, capped at $30,000 in trailing annual sales, and plans auto-upgrade as volume grows. There are no platform fees when you use an embedded payment provider, and a 2% fee on Core if you use another one. Catalyst, its reference storefront, is built on Next.js, React Server Components, and the Storefront GraphQL API, and deploys to Vercel.

Medusa is an open-source commerce framework in Node.js and TypeScript, with an MIT-licensed core and a commercial enterprise edition. SitePoint covered it when it was still a young Shopify alternative; it now has over 37,000 GitHub stars. Self-hosting is free. Medusa Cloud starts at $29 a month for development, $99 for launch, and $299 for scale, with no percentage of sales, and the tech giant claims you can export your data and self-host at any point.

Sources indicate that saleor is a GraphQL-native, API-only commerce platform written in Python and released under the BSD-3 license. Self-hosting is free. Saleor Cloud starts at $1,599 a month for up to $200,000 in monthly sales, with 0.8% on orders above that, and $3,999 a month at the next tier. It is built for teams with a dedicated engineering function and a large catalog, which is exactly who should pay that price.

It has been revealed that own only the storefront, and Shopify or BigCommerce will carry the rest. Own everything, and Medusa or Saleor give you a back end you can read. Already on WordPress, and WooCommerce is the obvious fit. Already have a storefront in Next.js or Astro and only need the money to move, and Whop is the shortest path. Whichever you pick, the checkout is where disputes start, so log what SitePoint's friendly fraud guide for developers recommends from day one.

A zoo in China has ‘given up’ on helping an overweight and viral leopard finally drop some pounds, admitting he is “too old” to help.

Industry observers note that you might think that just because an animal is in a zoo, it’s being fed perfectly and to a specific diet strategy. However, there are some animals that manage to pack on the weight and keep it on, no matter how much exercise they do.

Over in China, this has been the case for a few years with a leopard known as Pan Baobao. The 19-year-old leopard has gone viral a few times now, especially for his resemblance to Officer Clawhauser from the Zootopia franchise.

Keepers at the Panzhihua Zoo have, over the years, attempted to help the chunky predator lose a few pounds by changing his diet and getting him moving more. However, with the latest year approaching, they’ve decided to put an end to those attempts.

As per CNN Travel, a keeper told them that Pan Baobao has become too old to help him stick to a diet.

“He’s getting old, so weight loss isn’t advisable. The priority is to maintain his current condition and keep him healthy,” they said.

According to recent reports, an official at the zoo, Zhang Songwen, echoed this while speaking to First Post. “It’s not that we’re not controlling its diet, but it’s getting old and shouldn’t be losing weight,” Zhang added.

Keepers have noted that the significant cat is in “good condition,” and they just want to provide a comfortable life for Pan Baobao, who is still in “healthy spirits” too.

Elsewhere, vets in the United States helped a hawk get back to flying after initially diagnosing it as being “too fat.”.

Following on from the viral Cat Petting Simulator that lets you stroke virtual felines from the comfort of your mobile or desktop, Japanese developer zubu has created another contender: Pet The Horse.

As the name suggests, the browser game tasks you with stroking a horse’s head while it releases soft huffing sound effects. It’s pretty simple stuff, but it could be your new obsession to chill out with, particularly if you’ve just lost a race in Umamusume or been busy heisting your way through GTA 6.

Industry observers note that just like Cat Petting Simulator, you can pet up to six different colored horses using either your mouse or smartphone’s touchscreen. You can pet your chosen horse’s face, including their chin, mouth, mane, and can even scratch their ears for the real good stuff.

Industry observers note that the virtual horse will also respond to your petting, occasionally letting out cute sound effects. There’s even a night and day feature that you can change, with the night version dimming the screen and moving your virtual companion to a stable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A woman in Germany was slapped with a €25 ($27 USD) fine after sitting down on a bench at a children’s playground to cry, unaware that she was breaking the law by being there without a child.

The 31-year-old woman, identified as Hana, had gone for a walk through Glückaufpark in Gelsenkirchen on October 25 to clear her head after becoming overwhelmed by financial and academic pressures.

The chemistry student eventually broke down in tears, taking a seat on a bench at the playground and calling her aunt.

“I just wanted to be alone and not be seen by anyone,” she told German broadcaster WDR.

Sources indicate that however, three municipal enforcement officers approached her and asked whether two boys playing on the swings were her children. When she said no, the officers demanded her identification and issued her a €25 fine.

Under Gelsenkirchen’s municipal regulations, playgrounds are reserved for children aged 14 and under, along with their parents, guardians, and supervisors.

While there was a sign outlining the playground’s rules, BILD reports that it did not explicitly state that unaccompanied adults were prohibited from sitting on the benches.

Hana argued that the officers could have simply asked her to move instead of issuing a fine.

“I felt as though I was worth nothing as a human being,” she stated.

Despite criticism, the city defended the officers’ actions, describing the fine as relatively mild and proportionate. According to WELT, Hana has since paid the fine to avoid incurring additional costs.

Rather than relaxing the rules, the city council discussed increasing the maximum penalty for playground violations from €55 to €60 ($66) on November 17.
