A fashion reporter’s favorite things of 2026

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3066 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I’ll admit it.
  • According to recent reports, I’ll admit it.
  • But what most people don’t realize is that the job also involves a lot of squinting at fiber-content labels.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I’ll admit it. Being a fashion reporter can be a lot of fun. I get to sit across from some the most brilliant minds in the industry and peek at gorgeous collections seasons before they hit stores—long before they start shaping what we will wear. But what most people don’t realize is that the job also involves a lot of squinting at fiber-content labels. I’ve asked founders extremely nerdy questions about leather tanning methods. I’ve toured factories and tromped through cotton fields. Along the way, I come across many products. Over the course of a year, I wander through dozens of stores, wade through stacks of applications from brands hoping to land on our annual lists, and put bold fresh product claims to the test. Most of it is forgettable. But every so often, I come across something that I love: a clever jacket that is also beautiful, heels you can actually walk in all day, a pair of sneakers with a story so moving I still think about it months later. This list is the best of what I found in a year of poking, prodding, and road testing. If you’re shopping for someone who cares about style and quality, these are good bets. [Source Image: Resolute RGL] Every Stitch Tells a StoryResolute RGL, Najla in Olive Green, $350 Of the many products I reviewed this year, this is the one that made a biggest impression. Each Resolute sneaker carries a hand-embroidered panel of tatreez, the Palestinian cross embroidery that has passed down through generations. Each panel is stitched by a woman who lives in the villages in the South Hebron Hills of the West Bank. She chooses the pattern and colors herself, and a panel takes 14 to 24 hours to complete. The cooperative co-owns the tech giant, and embroiderers are paid as soon as their panels are finished. The shoes themselves are lovely, with an olive suede upper, memory foam insoles, and recycled rubber soles. They’re made to order and take eight to 10 weeks to arrive, so proposal ahead. [Source Image: Cole Haan] Light as a Feather, Tough Enough for a Nor’easterCole Haan, Grand Flex Fenella Buckle Lace-Up Waterproof Booties, $240 Most winter boots are heavy, adding weight as you trudge through the snow. Cole Haan has engineered these boots to be lightweight, but still set on a chunky lug sole that provides traction on icy sidewalks. They’re made from waterproof leather with sealed seams and a foam footbed that keep them cushy through a full day of walking. The buckle and laces give them a little edge, and a hidden ankle zip means you don’t have to do the laces again every time you leave the house. [Source Image: Parker Thatch] Mary Poppins Would Be Into ThisParker Thatch, Jack Tote in Leopard, $1,250 I am a person who carries too much: laptop, a novel, a snack, and a backup snack for my kids. The Jack allows overpackers to carry what they need for the day without looking like a duffel bag. It’s made from leopard-print hair-on cowhide with black leather trim and handles, and it fits a laptop with room to spare. There’s an interior zip pocket, two open pockets so your phone and glasses don’t get lost, and a snap closure. It’s the ideal gift for a professional woman in the market for a power bag. [Source Image: Lake] In-Law-Approved LoungewearLake, DreamModal Kimono Three-Piece Pants Set in Velvet Green Pencil Stripe, $168 The holidays involve lots of overnight guests, which can pose a dilemma. You want to be cozy, but you don’t want your in-laws to see you in your slinky nightgown or threadbare college T-shirt. Lake has many lounge sets. This one includes a wrap top with bell sleeves, a scoop-neck tank, and wide-leg pants with an elastic waist. It’s all made from a silky modal fiber, so it feels like you’re wearing pajamas but it looks like you’re in an outfit. The green and white stripe is festive without being kitschy. It’s machine washable, too. [Source Image: Margaux] Yes, You Can Walk in These HeelsMargaux, The Paloma Platform in Gold Nappa, $395 For years, most women assumed that “comfortable heels” is an oxymoron. Margaux is working hard to prove them wrong. The Paloma shoe has a 3.5-inch block heel, with a 1-inch platform, allowing you get the height without feeling unstable. There is plush foam padding under the sole and the straps are positioned so they don’t pinch. They’re handmade of nappa leather in Spain. I like the gold ones because they go with every holiday outfit. [Source Image: Maison de Sabré] Honey, I Shrunk the HandbagMaison de Sabré, The Mini Palais in Candy Plum, $675 Some nights call for nothing more than a phone, a lipstick, and a credit card. The Mini Palais is just big enough for these things, and its adjustable strap lets you wear it crossbody, on the shoulder, or in hand. The bags are also sustainable. Maison de Sabré skips conventional tanning, which is heavy on chemicals, in favor of DriTan, a waterless tanning technology. Each bag carries a serial number that allows you to trace it back to tanneries and farms in the Netherlands. And you can dress the bag up with adorable charms made from scraps of colorful leather discarded on the factory floor. [Source Image: Away] A Glamorous New Design from Away Away, The Aluminum Edge Carry-On, $428 Aluminum luggage has a certain glamour, but it’s heavy. Away’s new Aluminum Edge gives you a touch of aluminum on the frame and corners, but constructs the body out of a lighter polycarbonate shell that has a leather-like finish. It is full of luxurious touches, like champagne or nickel hardware. It closes with a lock, instead of a zipper, and it has a leather top handle. It comes in four colors, including a fun pink. [Source Image: Credo Beauty] Twelve Days of Clean BeautyCredo Beauty, Not Your Average Advent Calendar, $175 Credo, a retailer that stocks only nontoxic beauty brands, introduced an Advent calendar full of 12 full-size bestsellers (worth $445 in products) inside a blue beauty case. Some of my favorite products inside include a Westman Atelier lipstick, Saie’s mascara, and Nécessaire’s hand cream. There’s no waste in this Advent calendar. You’ll carry the toiletry bag around for years to come. [Source Image: Minnow] Swimwear for a Winter EscapeMinnow, Women’s Marigold Floral V-Neck One Piece, $218, and Marigold Floral Pareo, $128 If you’re lucky enough to be headed somewhere warm over the holidays, or you’re already dreaming about next year’s beach trip, this is what I’d pack. Minnow is a resort brand that makes thoughtfully designed swimwear. This summery set provides substantial coverage, while staying put so you can enjoy the pool with your kids. The matching pareo means you can wear the outfit to your hotel’s buffet breakfast before lounging poolside. (And if the whole family is coming along, the suit can be coordinated with matching styles for everybody.) [Source Image: Overland] A Functional, Beautiful JacketOverland, Kylie Reversible Sheepskin Jacket, $1,195 If you read my coats roundup this fall, you’ll recognize this jacket, made by Overland, which has been making sheepskin coats since 1973. I’m bringing it back because of all the jackets I tested this year, this one stood out. One side is a sleek leather jacket that has a strip of shearling peeking out at the collar. If you flip it inside out, it transforms into a plush shearling jacket. The pockets work from either side. It’s built to last, too, since sheepskin can last a lifetime with proper care. [Source Image: White + Warren] A Blanket-Like ScarfWhite + Warren, Cashmere Travel Wrap in Antique Gold, $385 Cashmere scarves are a traditional holiday gift, since they’re something anybody can appreciate. But this one stands out. It’s made of 100% cashmere but at almost 7 feet long, it works as a scarf, an evening wrap, or a full-body blanket on a red-eye. It can squish into a tote bag, but when you wear it, it feels substantial. It comes in a rainbow of colors; my favorite is the antique gold. [Source Image: Assouline] For the Bag Obsessive Who Has EverythingAssouline, Fashionphile: The Book of Iconic Bags, $120 Here’s a gift for the bag obsessive. Fashionphile, the luxury resale platform, knows exactly which bags hold their value and why. It has teamed up with Assouline to produce a silk-covered, 280-page tome about the 25 most influential handbags of all time, from the Hermès Birkin to the Fendi Baguette and the Dior Saddle, plus newer icons from Bottega Veneta and Loewe. It has more than 200 illustrations that will be eye candy to fashionistas. [Source Image: ME+EM] Three Earrings in OneME+EM, Transformer Earrings, $495 This piece of jewelry magically transforms to suit your outfit. The earrings start as gold-plated studs for the office. Clip on the detachable pendant and they become drops for dinner. The pendant is double-sided, with black marbled resin on one side and gold on the other, so you can flip it to suit your mood or your outfit. They’re made in Italy, and they work as well with a turtleneck as with a cocktail dress.

According to recent reports, after a national day of Thanksgiving, consumers have traditionally kicked off their holiday shopping on Black Friday. But are stores open and ready for it just one day after employees ate all that turkey? Here’s everything you need to know about what is open and closed on Black Friday. Is Black Friday a federal holiday? No, Black Friday is not a federal holiday, no matter what your shopaholic friends and family members may claim. Are banks open on Black Friday? Most banks are open on Black Friday, but some may have reduced hours because it is Thanksgiving week. Is the stock market open on Black Friday? Yes, both the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq are open, but both institutions close early, at 1:00 p.m. ET. Perhaps all those buyers and sellers need a nap after eating some Thanksgiving leftovers. Is the Post Office open on Black Friday? Is mail delivered? Yes. U.S. Postal Service post office locations will be back in action on Black Friday. Mail will also be delivered. Are FedEx and UPS delivering on Black Friday? Yes, UPS is back to normal on Black Friday. Some FedEx locations may have modified hours. Additionally, on-call and drop box pickups may be early. Are schools open on Black Friday? Most schools will be closed for Thanksgiving break but it is a good practice to double-check with your student’s institution. Are restaurants open on Black Friday? Most restaurants will be open to help fuel shoppers for a long day of deal hunting. Call ahead, though, to double-check your favorite mom-and-pop joint. It might take some time off. Are retail stores open on Black Friday? Absolutely. Retail stores such as Best Buy, Walmart, Target, and others desperately want your business. Many sales have already started online ahead of the substantial day. One notable exception is REI. For more than a decade, the outdoorsy store has promoted its “Opt Outside” initiative, remaining closed on Black Friday. Instead of shopping, it encourages people to take a hike, a walk, or do any outdoor activity. Are pharmacies open on Black Friday? Yes. Most pharmacies are open on Black Friday, including chains like CVS and Walgreens. Are grocery stores open on Black Friday? Yes, if you don’t have any Thanksgiving leftovers and need some grub, most grocery stores are open on Black Friday and happy to help. Membership-based stores like Costco and Sam’s Club will also be open.

#230496. The simplest well-being strategy leaders overlook

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1408 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

The simplest well-being strategy leaders overlook

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1408 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As leaders, we spend a lot of time thinking about employee well-being.
  • It has been revealed that as leaders, we spend a lot of time thinking about employee well-being.
  • Industry observers note that we know spending time in nature is good for us.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As leaders, we spend a lot of time thinking about employee well-being. I’ve found that supporting it often comes down to the everyday choices we make. That includes some of the simplest choices we tend to overlook. One of them is getting outside. We know spending time in nature is good for us. What’s striking is how hard it can be to do. The American Nature and Health Survey, which was supported by the REI Cooperative Action Fund in partnership with the Nature and Health Alliance, highlights this increasing disconnect. In the 2026 survey, Americans shared that nature is essential to their lives, yet we’re spending less time in it. A decade ago, 25% of respondents spent less than two hours a week in nature. Today, that number has nearly doubled to 45%. You can likely imagine why. Our lives are increasingly designed around convenience and screens. We can work, shop, connect, and entertain ourselves without ever stepping outside. Technology has made much of our lives easier and better, but it has also changed how we spend our time, often without us consciously making that choice.That matters because time in nature is linked to lower stress and better mental and physical health. And it doesn’t have to mean hours on the trail. Research suggests even 20 minutes outside can help us feel more centered, in mind and body. A RETAILER CLOSING ON BLACK FRIDAY For many people, there are real barriers to spending time outdoors, including access and safety. For others, it’s simply the competing demands of work and daily life. We still value nature, but too often, life makes it difficult to choose. That point has stuck with me as a business leader. There are plenty of things leaders can’t control. But we do have influence over how people spend their time at work and the conditions we create for people to do their best. With well-being, that means asking whether the way we work creates room for people to step away, recharge, and spend time outside. At REI Co-op, we’ve been exploring one version of that idea for more than a decade. In 2015, the co-op made an unusual choice for a retailer: We closed our stores on Black Friday, one of the most deeply ingrained traditions in American retail. We paid our employees to spend the day outside and encouraged customers to do the same. We called it Opt Outside. We didn’t tell employees how to spend the day or define what counted as “outside.” It could be a long hike, a walk through the neighborhood, time at a park with loved ones, or simply a quiet moment outdoors. The point was to create room for something that’s remarkably easy to push aside. MAKE CHOICES More than a decade since that first Opt Outside, I think there’s a leadership lesson in that choice, and it extends beyond REI. Not every company should do what we did. As leaders, we all make choices about what we make room for. Those choices don’t have to be big. Could your next one-on-one be a walk outside? Could a team gathering happen outdoors? Where in the workday could we make stepping outside, even for a few minutes, a little easier? These are small choices, but that’s the point. Supporting well-being and creating a better experience at work doesn’t always require another program or initiative. It starts with the everyday choices we make as leaders, and the things those choices make possible for others. CHOOSE TIME OUTSIDE This Black Friday, REI will once again close our stores and give our employees the day to spend outside. I’ll be doing the same, heading out for a hike with my family. One day outside doesn’t solve everything, and it’s not meant to. But after more than a decade of Opt Outside, at REI we still believe there’s value in choosing time outside. It has reinforced something for me about leadership: Our job is sometimes to look at what’s standing in the way of making different choices, and see what we can do to change it. Mary Beth Laughton is president and CEO of REI Co-op.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Sources indicate that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

Sources indicate that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Industry observers note that the ideal UI testing tool is the one that discovers what your users discover first: broken layouts, usability concerns that no longer work, and new accessibility issues in all the browsers your users use before a change goes into the repository. In 2026, most frontend teams don't rely on a single tool to do all of that. The best setups involve two layers: a test runner layer that launches the browser and monitors behavior, and a UI testing and review platform that visually checks the outcome and routes changes to the right stakeholders for sign-off.

According to recent reports, even with the right stack, it still relies on what your team needs to catch. Different teams will focus on different points: a QA team trying to automate checkout flows, a design system team defending shared components, and a single developer working on a tight budget will all be somewhere different. This guide is categorized by the job these UI testing tools do, then connects them.

Most "best UI testing tool" lists rank test runners and visual testing platforms against each other as if they were interchangeable. They aren't. UI testing covers four distinct jobs:.

Functional testing: Does the UI respond correctly when a user clicks, types, or hovers?

Visual testing: Does the UI still look right across layout, color, typography, and spacing?

Accessibility testing: Can people using keyboards and screen readers use it, and did this change introduce newly introduced violations?

Cross-browser and device coverage: Does it work in Safari on mobile, not just Chrome on a developer's laptop?

In a recent development, there are also other levels of UI tests. Unit tests test the logic but don't interact with the UI. End-to-end (E2E) tests represent the full user journey in a browser but are difficult to set up, hard to troubleshoot when the bug is a visual detail, and can't practically test every state. Between the extremes of unit tests and E2E tests, component tests simulate each component's behavior in a real browser using fixed inputs, offering speed closer to unit tests and user-level coverage closer to E2E. Many teams maintain a thin layer of E2E tests for critical journeys, and they have component tests for the dozens of states a component may be in.

These tools are organized by job so you can stack them rather than choose one winner.

These platforms sit on top of your test runner. They capture rendered UI, compare it to approved baselines, and give your team a place to review what changed.

Chromatic is a UI testing and review platform made by the Storybook team. It catches visual, interaction, and accessibility bugs in components and pages before they merge, and it gives developers, designers, and product managers one place to review UI changes and sign off. Chromatic's team is the core maintainer of Storybook, which has about 90,000 GitHub stars and 17 million weekly npm downloads, and a Vitest core maintainer on the team built Chromatic's Vitest integration. Chromatic is used by 45 Fortune 100 companies, including GitHub, Shopify, Microsoft, Adobe, the BBC, and monday.com.

Pricing: Free blueprint with 5,000 snapshots per month (Chrome only), unlimited projects and users. Starter is $179/month for 35,000 snapshots and adds Safari, Firefox, and Edge. Pro is $399/month for 85,000 snapshots. Enterprise is custom, with SSO, SCIM, SLA support, and data retention. TurboSnap snapshots count as 0.2 of a regular snapshot.

Trade-offs: Chromatic is strongest when your UI is built from components. Teams with no component tests can start from Playwright or Cypress E2E tests, but they'll get the most value once components are covered too. Snapshot usage also grows with each browser and viewport you add, so plan coverage before you scale it.

Best for: Design system teams, product teams that want designers and PMs to approve UI changes, React Native teams, and Vitest-first teams that want visual testing without baselines stored in the repo.

In a recent development, percy is BrowserStack's visual testing platform. It captures screenshots from your existing tests, renders them across browsers and responsive widths, and highlights pixel differences for review.

Strengths: Framework-agnostic SDKs for Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, and Storybook. App Percy covers native mobile apps. The free plan includes 5,000 screenshots per month with unlimited users and projects.

Industry observers note that trade-offs: Percy is page-oriented, and each page rendered in each browser at each width counts as a separate screenshot, so usage climbs promptly with cross-browser coverage. Percy compares feature branches against a base branch, which teams with complex branching should test early. Reviewers see rendered screenshots rather than an inspectable copy of the code under test, so debugging a diff usually means reproducing it locally.

Pricing: Free tier, then paid looks with fixed screenshot allowances and overage.

Best for: Teams already paying for BrowserStack that want visual checks on page-level E2E tests.

Applitools Eyes uses Visual AI to compare screenshots the way a person would, with match levels that can ignore content changes and focus on layout. Its Ultrafast Grid re-renders captured page states across many browser, viewport, and device combinations.

Strengths: Mature AI matching, broad browser and device coverage, Figma and Storybook testing, accessibility testing, and an MCP server. Higher tiers add AI-driven functional testing and plain-English test authoring.

Trade-offs: Applitools is priced and packaged for enterprises. There's a free trial but no free initiative, and the Starter plan is $667/month billed annually for 100,000 component checkpoints or 1,000 page checkpoints. Professional and Enterprise are custom-priced.

Best for: Large QA organizations with major cross-browser matrices and budget for a dedicated visual AI platform.

It has been revealed that backstopJS is a free, open-source visual regression testing tool released under the MIT license. You list the URLs, viewports, and CSS selectors to capture in a config file, and BackstopJS renders them in a headless browser through Playwright or Puppeteer, then compares the results against approved reference screenshots. The core workflow runs on three commands: backstop init, backstop test, and backstop approve.

Recent findings suggest that strengths: Completely free, with no screenshot limits. A built-in browser report reveals reference and test images side by side with a visual diff inspector, and changes can be approved from there. Optional Docker rendering keeps screenshots consistent between laptops and CI; Playwright adds Firefox and WebKit, and click, hover, and keypress selectors capture interactive states. JUnit reports plug into existing CI pipelines.

Trade-offs: BackstopJS is self-hosted, so there's no cloud dashboard, shared team review, or pull request status checks out of the box. Reference screenshots are usually committed to your repository, and every page or component state you want to test needs its own URL and scenario in the config. Someone on the team also has to own the setup, CI integration, and maintenance.

Best for: Developers and small teams with no budget who are comfortable running and maintaining their own visual regression setup.

According to recent reports, test runners click, type, and assert. They're free and open source, and every platform above builds on them. On their own, they offer limited visual testing: built-in screenshot assertions store baselines in your repository, rendering can drift between laptops and CI, and designers have no review interface.

Sources indicate that playwright is Microsoft's open-source browser automation framework. It runs tests across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, with auto-waiting, trace viewer debugging and code generation, and supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, and .NET.

According to recent reports, visual testing: Playwright's toHaveScreenshot assertion compares screenshots against baselines stored in Git. It works, but baselines must be regenerated per operating system, and accepting a change means rerunning with an upgrade flag.

Best for: Teams automating critical user journeys such as sign-up, checkout and login. Pair it with a platform like Chromatic for visual review across real browsers.

In a recent development, cypress is an open-source testing tool that runs inside the browser, with time-travel debugging that demonstrates the app at each step of a test. It supports both E2E and component testing.

According to recent reports, visual testing: Cypress has no built-in visual comparison and relies on plugins or a platform such as Chromatic, Percy or Applitools. Cypress Cloud, its paid service, adds recording, parallelization, flake detection and add-ons for accessibility and UI coverage.

Best for: Frontend developers who want fast feedback and an interactive test runner while they build.

Industry observers note that storybook is the open source workshop for building UI components in isolation. Each story captures one component state, and those stories double as test cases.

Testing features: Interaction tests with play functions and Testing Library, accessibility checks with the a11y addon, and a Vitest integration that runs stories as component tests.

Visual testing: Storybook doesn't diff screenshots on its own. Chromatic, built by the same team, is its visual testing and review layer.

Best for: Design system and component library teams, and any team practicing component-driven development.

Vitest Browser Mode runs component tests in a real browser instead of a simulated DOM, using Playwright or WebdriverIO under the hood.

It has been revealed that visual testing: Vitest's toMatchScreenshot assertion stores screenshots in the repository. For large projects, this can bloat the repo and baselines drift between machines. Chromatic can take Vitest Browser Mode tests with no code changes and run them in a stable cloud environment instead.

Best for: Teams already writing Vitest tests who want them to check how the UI looks without adopting a new framework.

Start from the problem your team is trying to fix:.

"Shared component changes keep breaking other teams' screens." Test at the component level with Storybook or Vitest Browser Mode and Chromatic, so the change shows up on the pull request that caused it.

"Our Playwright tests pass, but the layout still breaks in Safari." Functional assertions don't check appearance. Add a visual testing platform that renders in Safari, such as Chromatic, Percy or Applitools.

"We turned off screenshot tests because of false alarms." Look for deterministic component states and flake controls such as Chromatic's SteadySnap, or AI matching such as Applitools.

"Designers find UI bugs after release." Choose a platform with a review and approval workflow, and make sign-off a required pull request check.

"AI coding agents keep inventing components." Give agents access to your real component library, for example through Chromatic's hosted MCP, and run every agent-built change through the same UI tests as human code.

"We have no budget." Use Playwright or Vitest screenshot assertions, self-host BackstopJS, or start on the free tiers of Chromatic or Percy.

A practical, well-covered setup for a React web app looks like this:.

Unit tests in Vitest for logic and utilities.

Storybook stories or Vitest Browser Mode tests for every meaningful component state, with interaction tests on key components.

Chromatic running visual, interaction and accessibility tests on those components in Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge on every pull request, with designers assigned as reviewers.

A thin layer of Playwright E2E tests for sign-up, checkout and other critical journeys, also captured in Chromatic so page-level visual changes go through the same review.

This keeps most UI coverage in fast, deterministic component tests, while E2E tests confirm the journeys that matter most still work end to end.

In a recent development, playwright is the best free tool for E2E UI testing, and Storybook is the best free tool for testing component states. For visual testing, For visual testing, Chromatic and Percy both offer free tiers of around 5,000 snapshots or screenshots per month, and BackstopJS is free to self-host.

In a recent development, UI testing is the broad practice of checking that an interface works for users, including functional, visual and accessibility checks. Visual testing is one part of it: comparing rendered UI against approved baselines to catch unintended changes in layout, color, typography and spacing.

According to recent reports, no. Chromatic was built by the Storybook team, but it also runs visual tests from Vitest Browser Mode, Playwright and Cypress tests, and from React Native Storybook on iOS and Android simulators.

According to recent reports, playwright's toHaveScreenshot covers basic visual checks, but baselines live in your repo, rendering can differ between machines, and there's no review interface for designers. Teams with several reviewers or many browsers usually add a platform on top.

According to recent reports, most teams use both. Component tests cover individual UI states promptly and reliably, while a smaller set of E2E tests confirms that critical user journeys work across the whole app.

Black Friday 2026: These unexpected items are driving up U.S. consumer spending

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales.
  • retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales.
  • This year’s holiday shopping takes place in a U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The U.S. retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales. This year, the day once considered the holiday shopping season’s unofficial kickoff might look to spectators more like the fourth quarter of a football game.Brands and retailers have promoted steep discounts under the Black Friday banner all month, and some began rolling out deals before Halloween. But enough die-hard traditionalists hit the shops as soon as they can after Thanksgiving that the day remains the year’s biggest for foot traffic at physical stores, according to Sensormatic Solutions, a retail technology firm.“Black Friday is still the day for in-store shopping,” said Grant Gustafson, Sensormatic’s head of retail consulting and analytics.Stores also have kept drawing a majority of holiday season spending, although e-commerce captures a bigger share every year, according to U.S. Census data. Industry analysts expect the trend to continue; consumers spent $82.5 billion online from November 1 to November 22, a 9.1% increase from the comparable three weeks last year, according to research by Adobe.Retailers and consumers are giving Black Friday 2026 some other twists. The day’s evolution into a multiweek event has encouraged shoppers to stock up on discounted household basics while checking off their holiday lists, retail analysts said. Artificial intelligence and cost concerns are influencing how, where, when and on what consumers spend, retail analysts said.“It’s not just a moment where shoppers are buying gifts,” said Caila Schwartz, a retail and consumer insights leader at Salesforce. “They’re also buying things that they need, and so that’s going to help drive up a lot of the spend.”Here’s more on the emerging trends for Black Friday and holiday shopping overall: Low views of the economy aren’t expected to dim holiday sales This year’s holiday shopping takes place in a U.S. economic environment marked by voter frustration over gasoline prices fueled by the U.S. war with Iran, and high inflation overall.Analysts and economists scrutinize retail spending on the five days that begin with Thanksgiving Day and end on Cyber Monday for clues about consumers’ financial staying power and commercial prospects heading into the upcoming year.Retail sales were up and down all year as filling up a car and other nonnegotiable costs took more out of household budgets. Commerce Department figures for October showed Americans pulling back on buying books, clothes, sporting goods, and other items.The good news for retailers is that consumer confidence jumped this month as U.S. gas prices continued a steady decline.The National Retail Federation estimated that higher prices would account for about half of the 4.1% sales growth it expected in stores and online in November and December. The group forecast U.S. shoppers collectively spending $1.01 trillion. Black Friday still might have bigger discounts despite early deals U.S. retailers have broadly held the line on prices instead of making big increases across the board, and offered solid discounts that persuaded customers to shop earlier, industry analysts said.Salesforce, which tracks digital spending at a range of retailers, including grocery stores, said November discounts before Black Friday were 8% bigger than last year’s. Early promotions pushed average selling prices of physical merchandise 1% below last November’s prices, Salesforce said.Retailers nonetheless were likely to reserve their best prices for Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, Vivek Pandya, director of digital insights at Adobe, said.For example, discounts on TVs are expected to average 23% on Friday compared with 11% during the first 22 days of the month, according to Adobe. Shoppers are buying household items along with holiday gifts The deepest discounts between this past Tuesday and Monday were expected on clothing, home goods, and health and beauty, Salesforce said. The company said it expected health and beauty products to average 33% off.With Black Friday commencing well before the day itself, some consumers apply seasonal bargains to last long after the holidays by filling their cupboards with toiletries and clothes they would typically buy at another time, according to analysts.Online sales of personal hygiene products were 40% higher from November 1 through November 22 compared with the October average, according to Adobe’s data. Sales of household cleaning products spiked 33% and clothing basics by 27% during the same time frame, Adobe said.“Usually, when you think of holiday shopping, it’s premium handbags and jewelry and those types of items, but we’re fast seeing shoppers also use this season to stock up on the essentials,” Pandya said. AI tools may be persuading customers to do more online shopping Consumers are using AI-powered shopping tools to help them compare products and prices, particularly as inflation and paying more for gasoline have made them more attuned to price tags, Pandya said.Traffic to online retail sites from links in AI-powered tools more than doubled this month compared with November 2025, Adobe said.A belief that e-commerce sites will offer “the best value possible” has contributed to shoppers’ doing more of their holiday period spending online instead of in stores, Pandya said. —Anne D’Innocenzio, AP Retail Writer.

‘It was the talk of the playground’: Google’s AI features blocked by LA school officials

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2365 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • School districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices.
  • School districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices.
  • According to recent reports, schools are seeing growing backlash against technology, starting with cellphones and screentime and now focusing on AI, amid concerns that students are using AI to think for them.The Mountain View, California-based manufacturer in August found itself at the center of controversy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

School districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices. The move makes Los Angeles Unified the largest district to sideline the company, which has mentioned it will not separate its search product from AI tools for education.The LA district, which enrolls half a million students, has made no formal announcement, and the move caught parents and students by surprise, said Bridie Lee, a leader of Schools Beyond Screens LA, which has pushed for screen-time limits and tech oversight in the district.The group had several members who weighed in at a meeting of the Los Angeles school board’s A.I. committee on Friday, Nov. 13. By that Monday, AI Overview was gone.“It was the talk of the playground,” Lee said.Google is the dominant provider of education technology for America’s classrooms. Beyond its low-cost Chromebooks, the most widely used student laptops, Google’s suite of education apps like Google Docs and Classroom has become integral to classwork, homework and communication among students and teachers.But concerns about AI’s impact on learning have ignited a battle between schools and Google. In September, the country’s two largest school districts — New York and LA — revealed one-year moratoriums on student use of generative AI, and Google has said it’s not possible to take AI out of its search products. Schools are considering other internet search providers.LAUSD said in a statement it temporarily suspended AI Overview to ensure student experiences are “age-appropriate and safe.” It also said it continually evaluates its digital safeguards, including third-party tools. It was likely using such a tool that it was able to disable AI Overview.Schools Beyond Screens LA asked parents to send videos of what laptop screens looked like and received clips showing that AI Overview was no longer an option in Google search on district devices. Then activists reached out to the district, which confirmed AI Overview was disabled. Lee said they had no other details on how it was done or how long it is intended to stay disabled.“We’re thrilled LAUSD did this,” said Lee. “AI is seeping into everything. It’s dangerous. It’s hurting learning. And it’s a corporate overreach into public schools. It’s Substantial Tech attempting to strongarm tech policy without anyone’s consent.”Other districts, such as Fairfax County Public Schools in Virginia, have developed plug-ins to remove AI summaries for students searching on Google, according to multiple published reports. Google is increasingly at center of school tech backlash Schools are seeing growing backlash against technology, starting with cellphones and screentime and now focusing on AI, amid concerns that students are using AI to think for them.The Mountain View, California-based company in August found itself at the center of controversy. That’s when it said it had turned on its Gemini chatbot for many K-12 students using Google Classroom, its learning management system. Weeks later, New York City and LA schools banned generative AI. In New York, the ban applies to all elementary and middle school students, and in Los Angeles all students K-12 are banned from using AI on school devices. Both districts said the ban would allow officials to develop AI policies this academic year.Then, in early November, Google backtracked. It published a blog post saying it would instead turn off Gemini and all search tools by default for K-12 schools in the coming months. Administrators would have to turn on each tool if they wanted students to access them.Google said this was to give schools more choice. But the choice to turn off AI altogether is not there.While the blog post does not explicitly say search can’t be used without AI, Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times: “Search and AI are deeply integrated.” If schools ban AI, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”The integration of AI in search isn’t new. Google introduced AI Overview in 2025, and anyone who uses Google search will get AI answers to many search results. Google insists AI Overview is an integral part of its search product now and cannot be separated.Earlier this month, hundreds of Google employees signed a petition asking the company’s leadership to allow schools to turn off AI features “without disrupting their ability to use search as a whole.”“The way the decision has been reported in the press is poor, and makes Google, and our Education and Search products as a result, look like we’re punishing schools for not using AI,” the petition said. “Many students, educators and parents have concerns about AI in the classroom, as is shown by many school districts who have placed moratoriums or bans on such technology. It is our job as Googlers to respect the user, and listen to them when they have concerns about our products.” Google has made some changes — but not enough, activists say Google claims it hears parents’ and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to “shortcut learning” and that it shares the same goal: helping students learn. But what many parents and teachers want — the ability to bypass AI entirely and allow students to use Google search like it was in, say, 2024 — is not something Google offers. This has forced districts across the U.S. to choose between restricting students’ access to AI and maintaining access to the popular search engine.Instead of offering an AI-free search product for schools, Google announced a pilot “guided learning” tool that walks students “step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers.”“We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers,” the company said in a statement.Right now, Google search offers AI Overview, which contains summarized answers resulting from general searches, and AI Mode, which is a chatbot interaction. Guided learning, which is not yet available, will walk customers through steps intended to support critical thinking to get to the answer.LA schools had already disabled Google’s AI Mode at the beginning of the school year on school-issued student devices, said Jack Kelanic, the district’s chief information officer, during a school board committee meeting on artificial intelligence last week. Educators and staff still have access.“We understand this as a deeper embedding of AI into the education suite,” Kelanic said. He added, to applause, that the district is not bound to Google’s products if officials determine the changes are not in line with the district’s priorities.“We have choices,” Kelanic said. “We can change the default search engine literally overnight.” The Associated Press’ education coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. AP is solely responsible for all content. Find AP’s standards for working with philanthropies, a list of supporters and funded coverage areas at AP.org. —Barbara Ortutay, Jocelyn Gecker and Cheyanne Mumphrey, Associated Press.

Google insists AI Overview is an integral part of its search product now and cannot be separated.Earlier this month, hundreds of Google employees signed a petition asking the company’s leadership to allow schools to turn off AI features “without disrupting their ability to use search as a whole.”“The way the decision has been reported in the press is poor, and makes Google, and our Education and Search products as a result, look like we’re punishing schools for not using AI,” the petition said. “Many students, educators and parents have concerns about AI in the classroom, as is shown by many school districts who have placed moratoriums or bans on such technology. It is our job as Googlers to respect the user, and listen to them when they have concerns about our products.”.

According to recent reports, google says it hears parents’ and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to “shortcut learning” and that it shares the same goal: helping students learn. But what many parents and teachers want — the ability to bypass AI entirely and allow students to use Google search like it was in, say, 2024 — is not something Google offers. This has forced districts across the U.S. to choose between restricting students’ access to AI and maintaining access to the popular search engine.Instead of offering an AI-free search product for schools, Google announced a pilot “guided learning” tool that walks students “step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers.”“We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers,” the firm said in a statement.At the moment, Google search offers AI Overview, which contains summarized answers resulting from general searches, and AI Mode, which is a chatbot interaction. Guided learning, which is not yet available, will walk users through steps intended to support critical thinking to get to the answer.LA schools had already disabled Google’s AI Mode at the beginning of the school year on school-issued student devices, said Jack Kelanic, the district’s chief information officer, during a school board committee meeting on artificial intelligence last week. Educators and staff still have access.“We understand this as a deeper embedding of AI into the education suite,” Kelanic said. He added, to applause, that the district is not bound to Google’s products if officials determine the changes are not in line with the district’s priorities.“We have choices,” Kelanic said. “We can change the default search engine literally overnight.”.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is the highest-end model in Samsung’s 2026 Galaxy S26 lineup. Released back on March 11, it pairs a 6.9-inch display with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, a built-in S Pen, and a four-camera system led by a 200MP main sensor.

It’s a powerful device, built for photography enthusiasts and professionals who want to get the most out of their phones while on the go. You can apply protection to selected apps or sensitive notifications instead of obscuring everything all the time. That’s useful when checking messages on a train or opening personal information in a busy restaurant.

In our Galaxy S26 Ultra review, we talked about how the Privacy Display is flexible and useful, able to be enabled for certain apps and left off for others.

We also found dependable everyday endurance from the 5,000mAh battery, and now that the phone supports 60-watt wired charging, quick top-ups become more useful. Samsung also promises seven generations of OS upgrades and seven years of security updates from launch, an important consideration if you initiative to keep your next phone for several years.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra’s main advantages over the Galaxy S26 and S26+ are Privacy Display, the integrated S Pen, and its more versatile camera hardware.

According to recent reports, at launch, US pricing started at $899.99 for the Galaxy S26, $1,099.99 for the Galaxy S26+, and $1,299.99 for the Galaxy S26 Ultra, each with 256GB of storage. But those prices have dropped over the past few months, and you may be able to get them for less. We’ve seen the S26 Ultra, for example, as low as $999.99 during Prime Day.

Having different lenses gives you more options for portraits, travel photos, and subjects you can’t easily walk closer to.

The regular Galaxy S26 is the more natural choice if you prioritize a smaller phone and a lower purchase price. The Galaxy S26+ makes sense if you want a large-screen Galaxy without paying for Ultra-specific features.

The biggest improvement since launch is the move from Android 16-based One UI 8.5 to Android 17-based One UI 9.

In a recent development, one UI 9 offers several practical additions. Now Nudge suggestions extend beyond the keyboard into conversation notifications and a floating button. In a recent development, the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s features are most useful when they solve problems or make everyday moments feel joyful and seamless. Here are five examples:.

If you’re coming from a Galaxy S22 or S23 series phone, there are so many upgrades, small and large, that are awaiting you with the S26 Ultra.

Google’s Fitbit Air is one of my favorite products of 2026 and my preferred workout companion, but not being able to see a workout while you’re in the middle of it has been a huge complaint of mine, and the latest Google Health upgrade is fixing that.

Quite literally at the start of this week, I was on a walk through my neighborhood and though to myself, “it’s still pretty annoying that I can’t see my workout progress in the Google Health app.” It’s been a complaint of mine for a while, as various treadmill sessions and more have left me wondering what my heart rate is looking like, how many steps I’ve taken, etc, and it’s only a problem when using the Fitbit Air, seeing as the Pixel Watch (or Fitbit Edge) I’d wear otherwise will show that data front and center.

Google Health 5.13 is fixing that.

It has been revealed that in the changelog for Google Health 5.13, Google details a fresh “exercise in-progress” card on the main “Today” screen. This will show what exercise is being tracked and also let you end the workout early.

Sources indicate that if you use your Pixel Watch, Fitbit Air, or Fitbit Edge to automatically track your exercises, you’ll now see an exercise-in-progress card on your mobile app’s Today screen. This card lets you know that your device is tracking your exercise and gives you the opportunity to end the tracking and get your summary whenever you want.

We don’t know exactly what this card looks like just yet, but it sounds like it fits the need perfectly.

Google Health 5.13 is now rolling out on Android and iOS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

It has been revealed that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

It has been revealed that adding real-time video to a web app used to mean plugins, proprietary SDKs and a lot of money. Today every modern browser ships with WebRTC, a set of APIs that lets two browsers exchange audio, video and data directly. The catch is that WebRTC gives you building blocks, not a finished feature. This guide walks through those blocks in the order you actually need them, with the exact API calls you need, and then covers the production challenges that tutorials usually skip.

A browser-to-browser call has four moving parts:.

Industry observers note that start with the local preview. Browsers only allow camera access on HTTPS or localhost, so serve your page accordingly.

1. Request a stream with navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(), passing video constraints (an ideal width of 1280 and height of 720 is a sensible default) and audio constraints with echoCancellation and noiseSuppression enabled.

In a recent development, 2. Assign the returned MediaStream to the srcObject property of your local video element.

According to recent reports, 3. Keep a reference to the stream, because you will add its tracks to the peer connection later.

Recent findings suggest that set the muted and playsinline attributes on the local video element. Without muted users hear themselves, and without playsinline iOS Safari opens the video full screen.

The peers need a way to find each other. A tiny Node.js server using the ws package is enough for development. Its whole job is to relay messages between the peers in a room:.

1. Create a WebSocket server (for example with the ws package) listening on its own port.

Sources indicate that 2. Keep a map of room names to the set of sockets in each room.

3. When a client sends a join message, store the room name on the socket and add it to that room's set.

4. For every other message type, forward the raw message to the other sockets in the same room, and never echo it back to the sender.

5. On disconnect, remove the socket from its room so stale peers do not receive messages.

In production you would add authentication, limit room size to two for one-to-one calls, and validate message types, but the shape stays the same.

Both sides create an RTCPeerConnection, add their local tracks and listen for the remote ones:.

1. Create a new RTCPeerConnection with an iceServers list that contains at least one STUN server.

Sources indicate that 2. Loop over the local stream's tracks and call addTrack() for each one.

3. In the ontrack handler, attach the first remote stream to your remote video element.

4. In the onicecandidate handler, send every upcoming candidate to the other peer through your signalling channel as a candidate message.

Industry observers note that one peer creates an offer, the other answers, and both apply each other's descriptions. Candidates arrive asynchronously in the background.

Industry observers note that 1. The caller runs createOffer(), applies it with setLocalDescription() and sends the description as an offer message.

Industry observers note that 2. The callee applies the offer with setRemoteDescription(), runs createAnswer(), applies it locally and sends it back as an answer.

Recent findings suggest that 3. The caller applies the answer with setRemoteDescription().

4. Both sides pass every incoming candidate message to addIceCandidate().

If both peers might start a call at the same time, look up the "perfect negotiation" pattern on MDN. It assigns one side as polite and resolves offer collisions cleanly instead of leaving both peers stuck.

On a home network, STUN alone often works. On corporate Wi-Fi, mobile carriers and symmetric NATs it frequently does not, and the call silently fails to connect. A TURN server relays media when a direct path is impossible. The open-source coturn server is the usual choice.

In practice, your iceServers list should contain your own STUN URL plus a TURN URL with a username and credential, so the browser can fall back to the relay automatically when direct connectivity fails.

Generate short-lived TURN credentials on your backend rather than hard-coding them, and budget for bandwidth: relayed calls pass every frame through your server.

Users deny camera access, unplug headsets and switch from Wi-Fi to 4G mid-call. Catch NotAllowedError and show a clear explanation, listen for devicechange events, and use RTCRtpSender.replaceTrack() to swap cameras without renegotiating the whole call.

In a recent development, listen to pc.onconnectionstatechange. When the state becomes disconnected, wait a few seconds before giving up, because it often recovers. On failed, call pc.restartIce() to try fresh network paths.

In a recent development, use RTCRtpSender.setParameters() to cap the bitrate on weak connections, and read pc.getStats() to monitor packet loss and round-trip time. Showing a small "poor connection" indicator does more for perceived quality than any codec tweak.

Mesh calls, where every participant connects to every other, work for two or three people. Beyond that, upload bandwidth explodes. Group calls need a Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) such as mediasoup, LiveKit or Janus, which receives each stream once and forwards it to the others.

Tutorials end at a working demo, but the fastest way to understand what production WebRTC looks like is to watch a real call from the inside. Chrome ships an internal diagnostics page that shows every peer connection the browser opens, and it works on any site that uses WebRTC.

Industry observers note that 1. Open chrome://webrtc-internals in one tab and keep it open.

2. In another tab, start a call on your own demo and find its RTCPeerConnection entry.

Sources indicate that 3. Expand that entry and look at the ICE candidate pairs: you will see whether the call went direct (host or srflx) or through a TURN relay (relay).

Industry observers note that 4. Open the stats graphs for the outbound video stream and watch the bitrate, frame rate and resolution adapt when you throttle the network in DevTools.

5. Check the negotiated codec and how rapidly the connection recovers when you switch Wi-Fi off and back on.

Once you can read your own call, repeat the exercise on a production service. Any browser-based product works, whether a meeting tool or a live video chat that pairs two visitors, because webrtc-internals shows the same data for every site. Expect differences from your demo: more candidate pairs, a relay candidate in the list and a bitrate that adapts faster. Seeing them makes the earlier sections concrete, from why TURN matters to how bandwidth estimation reacts to packet loss.

Recent findings suggest that the one-to-one call above is the core of many products, from telehealth consultations and tutoring to customer support. The engineering challenges grow with the use case: random matching needs queueing and presence on the signalling server, public platforms need moderation and reporting, and global audiences need TURN servers in several regions.

According to recent reports, start with the minimal version, get it working across Chrome, Firefox and Safari on both desktop and mobile, and add TURN before real customers arrive. Once the call is reliable, every other feature becomes a much easier problem.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tenebrae Lux is a gag that has inspired some larger conversations about the gap between indie games and big-budget blockbusters.

Tenebrae Lux is a gag that has inspired some larger conversations about the gap between indie games and massive-budget blockbusters.

It has been revealed that one of the most intriguing games of the year is called Tenebrae Lux. It’s a moody, black-and-white title with obtuse puzzles and a main character that constantly narrates to himself with dramatic language. Its credits attribute pretty much everything to a developer named Johannes Zuch. It’s generated a lot of discussion for seemingly mocking games like Jonathan Blow’s The Witness or The Chinese Room’s Dear Esther. It’s also a game that only exists inside of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Developer Rockstar Games has stuffed a lot of satirical media inside of GTA VI, including TV shows you can watch, books you can read, and radio shows you can listen to. It’s all in service of making the world feel like a funhouse-mirror version of our current reality — Ted Lasso star Jason Sudeikis plays a right-wing radio host, for example. There are more games you can play inside GTA VI in addition to Tenebrae Lux, including a zombie-themed roguelike. But Tenebrae Lux, which you have to see as part of GTA VI’s main story, is the one that has struck a chord, including with indie developers like Sam Barlow and Robert Yang.

“I have to admit it’s kind of funny for the biggest blockbuster game of all time to go after arthouse indie,” Yang tells The Verge, noting that it’s “like a fighter jet getting obsessed with an ant, petty in a funny way.” (Given that GTA VI earned $3.79 billion in its first day, the gulf between Rockstar and indie game studios that are struggling to get by is vast.).

Sources indicate that but Yang suggested that Rockstar developers are probably well versed in the types of games they’re lampooning in GTA VI. “I don’t think gamers understand how much indie experimental stuff any decent AAA dev plays,” Yang noted, pointing out that Rockstar’s environmental artists and level designers “all probably love Dear Esther,” the influential first-person game that helped popularize the “walking sim” concept when it debuted in 2012.

Sources indicate that “I was mostly taken with what it meant that the millions of people playing the game were having to sit down and play through an extended gag about indie games,” Barlow tells The Verge. “That made me feel like we were part of larger culture.” He added that he hopes some of these players might “seek out what these arty indie games might be.”.

Industry observers note that rockstar is self-aware enough to use its video games to poke fun at the medium itself. As part of a long conversation between protagonist Jason Duval and his friend Cal Hampton before they start playing Tenebrae Lux, Cal hypes the game by saying that none of it is “just sitting around waiting for people to finish talking.” Initially, you only play Tenebrae Lux for a few minutes, which is enough time to get stumped on the initial puzzles, before the game cuts back to Jason being bored. “Got anything else, a little less, uh… y’know?” he asks. They play the zombie game, titled Street Trash 3 Dezombifier, right after. (You can go back and play the entirety of Tenebrae Lux later if you want.).

Recent findings suggest that barlow stated that the cut “felt very true to the character and story. I gather there is more to the game, but it felt natural to me to hit a wall with the pretentious puzzle design and then move on!”.

According to recent reports, yang also pointed out that from a design perspective, GTA VI has more in common with Tenebrae Lux than Street Trash 3 Dezombifier. GTA VI is “basically a walking sim where you walk around Florida and listen to people talk,” Yang said. “What’s the difference? Well, just like a billion dollars I guess.”.

Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.

Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one massive effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.

It has been revealed that leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.

PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.

It has been revealed that at this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

A new leak suggests that Samsung is preparing to copy the iPhone’s Dynamic Island feature in the not-too-distant future, to an extent that not many other Android brands have even done thus far.

Copying the Dynamic Island was briefly like a rite of passage for some Android brands, with many wasting almost no time in delivering their own version of the feature. But, on many of those devices, it’s a surface-level ripoff at best. The feature is primarily limited to music apps and timers, rarely working with any third-party apps in meaningful ways. Android has a built-in feature similar to Apple’s but not in the same styling.

Samsung is now preparing its own version of the Dynamic Island, and it seems this one has a bit more meat on its bones.

Recent findings suggest that samMobile on Twitter/X posted a video and two still images of what appears to be a Dynamic Island clone coming to Galaxy devices. It’s mentioned as potentially coming to the Galaxy S27 series (so, One UI 9.5) and being called “Moment Effects.” A portion of the software explicitly mentions integration with Google Sports, the leak claims, while it seems Samsung is using Live Notifications here, which already support a number of third-party apps.

The current implementation of live activities showing the "chip" in the top bar is honestly far from good.

It negates one of the major pros of Android over iOS: being able to see notification icons in the top bar.

As when the "chip" of the live activity is active/shown, all notification icons will get hidden, even if there's a ton of space left between the "chip" and the constraint of the front camera area - an implementation that makes no sense whatsoever.

I honestly can't fathom how could Google come out with such poor implementation.

I don't particularly like this one from Samsung, but it surely is 1000000 times better from a UX perspective.

The kicker from a UX perspective is that Samsung’s interpretation allows you to swipe between activities, similar to Apple, but the core premise is similar with the island showing around the selfie camera cutout.

It has been revealed that when this feature might surface does remain unclear, but a One UI 9.5 debut would make plenty of sense. That upgrade is in beta now and due to launch on the Galaxy S27 series early next year.

It has been revealed that what do you think of Samsung’s alleged Dynamic Island clone? Personally, I’m on board as long as it proves useful, and it seems to be on the right track compared to most other copycats.

#230476. Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1200 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 The Verge ↗ Open Full Page

Why GTA VI’s version of Florida feels so real

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1200 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Virtual city expert Emma Fraser explains what makes Rockstar’s latest open world work.
  • It has been revealed that there are plenty of reasons why Grand Theft Auto VI is so popular: the 13 years of anticipation, the relatable lead characters and romantic storyline, the sheer level of depth.
  • Industry observers note that “There’s something about this particular game that is really discombobulating and distracting in a sense,” she notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Virtual city expert Emma Fraser explains what makes Rockstar’s latest open world work.

It has been revealed that there are plenty of reasons why Grand Theft Auto VI is so popular: the 13 years of anticipation, the relatable lead characters and romantic storyline, the sheer level of depth. But another major factor is the sense of place. The GTA series is unmatched when it comes to re-creating the feeling of a bustling, real-world city, and GTA VI’s fictional rendition of Florida is the studio’s most lifelike setting yet. It has functioning buses and trains, plentiful buildings you can go into and explore, residents you can chat with, and huge areas where you can interact with wildlife far away from the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City. For Emma Fraser, an assistant professor at UC Berkeley who studies urban ruins and virtual cities, the sense of realism has created a unique sensation while playing.

Industry observers note that “There’s something about this particular game that is really discombobulating and distracting in a sense,” she notes. “Because you have these moments where you think, ‘I’m in a place, I’m experiencing a location.’ You comprehend intellectually that it’s not real or that it’s at best a representation, but you still have this feeling in your brain and you’ll still dream about being in that place.”.

Fraser teaches courses on topics including urban geography and virtual worlds and has written papers exploring topics like “mapping in the digital age” and “the virtual spectacle of the end of the city.” She says she started researching video game cities in part because, despite their influence and reach, they’re an underexplored space in academia. “I’m a geographer, and geographers are obsessed with cities,” she explains. “So much of geography is thinking about: How do we imagine cities? How do we navigate cities? How do we build cities? How do we map cities? And video games have all of that, but they’re not taken that seriously as an academic interest.”.

According to recent reports, like much of the world, she’s been looking forward to GTA VI for years, particularly because of Rockstar’s on-the-ground approach to research. Before development on the game began, developers from the studio traveled to Florida to get an accurate picture. As GTA VI producer Rob Nelson told me, the starting point for the game was the setting, rather than the story or characters. “We just went around to feel it out,” he mentioned. “Go to the Everglades, go to the Keys, go to the city, as many places as we can, and start thinking about what aspects of the place we want to incorporate.”.

Recent findings suggest that while there are plenty of open-world games, many of the most successful — from Elden Ring to The Witcher — are sent in fantastical spaces. GTA stands apart in how its various settings look and feel true to the real world. And Fraser believes that this is one of the key reasons the series has such universal appeal. “You know immediately how to function in a city,” she explains. “You know there’s going to be law enforcement, there are going to be city blocks, there are going to be pedestrians, cars, and buses. It’s this really interesting environment that gives you a lot of possibilities to get a player more immersed in your world, because they already know a lot about a city as a general concept.”.

“You can’t hold a whole city in your mind at one time.”.

In a recent development, fraser describes GTA VI’s world as having “implied expansiveness.” It’s not a one-to-one re-creation of the real location. There are plenty of things missing; you don’t see schools or daycares, and parking spaces are relatively sparse. But the game gets enough details right to be recognizable. Fraser explains that as long as certain parts of the city look correct — the lighting, the coastline, the decoration of street corners, the major arterial roads — that’s enough to convince people that they’re in something resembling Miami.

“You can’t hold a whole city in your mind at one time,” she says. “Instead it’s these highlights. What [Rockstar] do very successfully in the game is those snapshots. They’ve got far more content that is recognizable as Florida or Miami than they’ve been able to fit into previous games. So it’s a much more overwhelming sense of being in that place.” The “implied expansiveness” also comes in the form of dialogue, radio programs, and TV shows that suggest a much bigger world by discussing places and moments that exist outside of the game you can actually explore.

This level of verisimilitude — combined with the fact that players can explore the city from multiple perspectives, everything from walking to flying a plane — has led to an experience that Fraser likens to virtual tourism, which can result in all kinds of different playstyles. “Some tourists are going to blow a lot of money on taxis and get to wherever they’re going as fast as they can,” she explains, “and some people just like sitting on a bus or a train and getting to know a place.” Similarly, there are certain players who will just experience the story and play through the main missions, and others who will get lost in side activities like bird watching.

“Some people just like sitting on a bus or a train and getting to know a place”.

What’s also notable about GTA VI is how its relationship-focused premise is motivating some players to experience the world in a much less violent way. And that includes how they move through the city. Some people are driving more carefully to avoid killing civilians, while others are exploring spaces while both characters hang out together. “In the first few games, you’re this empty vessel. You’re a criminal, you’re doing criminal things,” says Fraser. “Whereas with GTA VI your motivation and the way you think about your character is really important.”.

It has been revealed that now that the game is out and millions of players are venturing through Vice City, Fraser is hoping to use it to research the ways that real and virtual worlds intersect when it comes to how we navigate cities. GTA VI offers a lot of choice in this regard; you can still steal a Lambo and speed through the streets, but you can also hop on a train, put on some headphones, and listen to a podcast while getting where you need to be. “Because this world is so fully furnished, and you have so many options, you might start to import your own real-world practices into the game,” she notes.

Industry observers note that but at this point, what has struck her most is the attention to detail that separates the universe of GTA VI from its contemporaries. “You can’t just generate a generic city and stick icons in, which is what a lot of games do,” she explains. “You aren’t going to get a sense of a real place if you do it that way.”.
